Steve's Roc Workroc-syntax-colorShale on GitHub

Roc on Shale

The programs on this page are written in Roc and run on Shale, a runtime for programs that work with files, folders and other programs. Each is a check or a report we run on our own code, shown in full.

What Roc brings

Roc is a fast, friendly, functional language.

  • Fast. Roc compiles to machine code.
  • Checked. The type checker infers every type, so a program needs few annotations and still has every call checked before it runs.
  • Pure by default. A function that reads a file is marked by its name and its type. Everything else is plain computation that a test can call directly.
  • Tested in place. Tests are expects, written beside the code they test.

Effects come from a platform

Every Roc application runs on a platform, which supplies its effects: reading files, reaching the network and the rest. A program has only the effects its platform offers. basic-cli, Roc's standard platform for command-line programs, offers a wide set: files and folders, the network, environment variables, the clock and more. The platform these examples use offers a narrower set, adds a few things of its own, and has Shale's runtime as its host, so each effect is a call into Shale, held to the limits Shale sets for the run. Everything else is plain Roc.

What it offers

  • Files: read and write a file, ask whether one exists, list, make and remove a folder, glob and grep.
  • Programs: run one, with a timeout, keeping the head, the tail or the whole of its output.
  • The rest: print, stop with a message, and read the script's arguments.

What it adds

  • Roc's parse tree. roc_tree! hands a program Roc's own parse of a file, so a check reads Roc code as Roc reads it.
  • Regular expressions, supplied by the host.
  • Shale's limits on every effect: budgets for a run's steps, reads and output; reads only beneath the run's root and its named mounts; a program run only when Shale's rules allow it; and a timeout on each one.

Beyond this platform

basic-cli also offers the network, environment variables, standard input and the clock. The programs here need only what's listed above. The platform's README explains how it works.

The examples

The examples are in sections. The first holds programs that find flaws in Roc code, and one that fixes them too: Roc reading Roc, most of them through Roc's own parser. After it come programs that read Shale itself, then reports on Roc projects, then smaller programs over Zig. The shared packages the examples import are shown once, at the end.

Shale's own language

Shale is also a scripting language of its own, and each example began as a Shale script. Each Roc program is followed by the Shale script it was ported from, with both files colored by roc-syntax-color. Each port was checked against its original's output. The links at the top and end of each example go to the one before or after it.

How the runtime is built

Shale's runtime is written in C, in its repository's c/ folder, and needs only Linux on x86-64, GCC and TCC.

  • One translation unit. c/shale.c takes in the whole runtime, so GCC sees every function at once and the release build is a single gcc -O2.
  • Two compilers. TCC compiles the whole program in a fraction of GCC's time, for the edit loop. GCC builds every binary we ship, with no LLVM involved.
  • Two tiers of checks. The fast tier runs every C test in seconds, on each edit. The full tier adds the release build, every test under ASan and UBSan, a -Werror build at -O2, and the cookbook's own tests, including the goldens behind the examples below. It runs on GitHub, before every merge. Each test was also proven once, by a planted fault, to be able to fail.
  • The builds are Shale scripts. A new machine builds its first shale by hand with TCC and GCC, and from then on Shale builds itself.

The Roc platform's host is that same C, with a small driver added. It's compiled once with gcc -O2 into an object and cached. Each Roc script is built by the pinned Roc compiler into an archive and linked with that object, and the program is cached by a hash of every file it's built from. The Roc runs on a stack of its own, takes its memory from an arena held to the run's budget, and has a CPU budget for its own computation.

Finding and fixing flaws in Roc code

The checks that Steve's Roc repositories run in their gates, ported from Shale to Roc, so each one is Roc code reading Roc code, most of them through Roc's own parser.

find_unclear_names

A gate over Roc's own parse trees for names and module docs that say too little: a pure function named like a mutation, an abbreviation, a missing or historical doc.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_find!, Shale.re_lines!, Shale.re_replace!, Shale.read!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!.
Roc: 752 lines in 5 files. Shale original: 372 lines, plus 1,374 lines in the 6 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Declarations, Finding, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names/find_unclear_names.roc, 192 lines

## find_unclear_names, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## names and top comments that say less than they should. Its launcher,
## cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names.shale, is how it is run, and its header
## says the rules, `pure_mutator`, `abbreviation` and `module_doc`.
## check_goldens.shale, beside this, holds its output on the plants to its
## goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale glob=app/**/*.roc
##   shale cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `abbreviations`, `words`, `accepted`,
## `terms`, `house` (`house=0` leaves out the house style, `abbreviation`) and
## `self_test` (`self_test=1` runs the plants, each through the launcher).
##
## This root reads the word lists, runs each check on each file and prints
## the verdict. Its modules are beside it: one a check (PureMutator,
## Abbreviation, ModuleDoc) and SelfTest. What they read (Tree, Declarations,
## Text) and Finding are the cookbook's Roc library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 roc_cpu_ms=600000 programs=100
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import Abbreviation
import ModuleDoc
import PureMutator
import SelfTest

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	if Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1" {
		SelfTest.run!(checks)
	} else {
		verdict = run_check!({})
		if !(List.is_empty(verdict.found)) {
			Shale.fail!(verdict.summary)
		}
	}
}

# ── The word lists ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

read_word_list! : Str => Str
read_word_list! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("no word list ${path}")
			""
		}
	}

## A list of one word per line, any note after `--` cut off, as a set. A
## word listed twice, or a line of two words, stops the run.
word_set! : Str => Set(Str)
word_set! = |path| {
	var $set = Set.empty()
	for l in Text.lines(read_word_list!(path)) {
		word = Str.trim(Text.before_first(l, "--"))
		if Str.contains(word, " ") or Set.contains($set, word) {
			Shale.fail!("${path}: `${word}` is no single new word")
		}
		if word != "" {
			$set = Set.insert($set, word)
		}
	}
	$set
}

## The accepted terms file: a term a line, each with its reason after `--`.
## A line without a reason stops the run.
accepted_terms! : Str => Set(Str)
accepted_terms! = |path| {
	for l in Text.lines(read_word_list!(path)) {
		parts = Str.split_on(l, "--")
		term = Str.trim(List.first(parts) ?? "")
		reason = Str.trim(List.get(parts, 1) ?? "")
		if term != "" and reason == "" {
			Shale.fail!("${path}: `${term}` has no reason after `--`")
		}
	}
	word_set!(path)
}

# ── The run ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## Whether `house=0` leaves the house style out (cookbook/roc/house.shale).
house_is_off! : {} => Bool
house_is_off! = |{}| {
	house = Shale.arg!("house", "1")
	if house != "0" and house != "1" {
		Shale.fail!("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not ${house}")
	}
	house == "0"
}

## The checks, in the order the summary counts them.
checks : List(Str)
checks = ["pure_mutator", "abbreviation", "module_doc"]

## The summary and the finding lines, sorted (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `verdict_of`).
verdict_of : List(Finding), U64 -> { summary : Str, found : List(Str) }
verdict_of = |report, file_count| {
	sorted = List.sort_with(report, Finding.order)
	found = sorted.map(Finding.line_of)
	{ summary: "find_unclear_names (Roc): ${U64.to_str(file_count)} files; ${Finding.counts_of(sorted, checks)}", found }
}

run_check! : {} => { summary : Str, found : List(Str) }
run_check! = |{}| {
	abbreviations = word_set!(Shale.arg!("abbreviations", "cookbook:words/abbreviations.txt"))
	words = word_set!(Shale.arg!("words", "cookbook:words/short_words.txt"))
	accepted_here = accepted_terms!("cookbook:words/accepted_terms.txt")
	project_accepted = Shale.arg!("accepted", "")
	accepted = if project_accepted == "" {
		accepted_here
	} else {
		Set.union(accepted_here, accepted_terms!(project_accepted))
	}
	lists = { abbreviations, words, accepted }
	terms_file = Shale.arg!("terms", "")
	terms = if terms_file == "" {
		Set.empty()
	} else {
		word_set!(terms_file)
	}
	paths = Shale.glob!(Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc"))
	var $report = []
	var $refused = []
	for f in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if f.err != "" {
			$refused = $refused.append(
				if Str.starts_with(f.err, f.path) {
					f.err
				} else {
					"${f.path}: ${f.err}"
				},
			)
		} else {
			src = match Shale.read!(f.path) {
				Found(text) => Str.split_on(text, "\n")
				Missing => []
			}
			declared = Declarations.from_file({ path: f.path, nodes: f.nodes, source_lines: src })
			aliases = List.fold(
				declared.types,
				Dict.empty(),
				|m, d| if !(d.is_nominal) {
					Dict.insert(m, d.name, d.underlying)
				} else {
					m
				},
			)
			for d in declared.values {
				$report = List.concat($report, PureMutator.judge(f.path, d, aliases, terms))
			}
			if !(house_is_off!({})) {
				$report = List.concat($report, Abbreviation.judge(f.path, f.nodes, declared, lists))
			}
			$report = List.concat($report, ModuleDoc.judge!(f.path, f.nodes, declared, src))
		}
	}
	verdict = verdict_of($report, List.len(paths))
	summary = if house_is_off!({}) {
		"${verdict.summary}; left out as house style: abbreviation"
	} else {
		verdict.summary
	}
	print_findings!(summary, verdict.found)
	if !(List.is_empty($refused)) {
		for r in $refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${r}")
		}
		Shale.fail!("find_unclear_names: roc-ast refused ${U64.to_str(List.len($refused))} files (named above), which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged")
	}
	{ summary, found: verdict.found }
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale).
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, found| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(List.is_empty(found)) {
		for l in found {
			Shale.print!(l)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names/Abbreviation.roc, 191 lines

## The `abbreviation` check: a name with a word short for another, read from
## every name a file gives or says (the launcher's header says the rule).
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

Abbreviation := [].{

	## The word lists the check reads: the abbreviations, the English words
	## of two to four letters, and the accepted terms.
	Lists : { abbreviations : Set(Str), words : Set(Str), accepted : Set(Str) }

	## The findings of the file at `path`, a name once a file.
	judge : Str, List(Tree.Node), Declarations, Abbreviation.Lists -> List(Finding)
	judge = |path, tree, declared, lists| {
		var $seen = Set.empty()
		var $report = []
		for given in names_given(path, tree, declared) {
			if !(Set.contains($seen, given.name)) {
				$seen = Set.insert($seen, given.name)
				found = Text.name_words(given.name).keep_if(|w| is_abbreviated(w, lists))
				if !(List.is_empty(found)) {
					$report = $report.append({ path, line: given.line, check: "abbreviation", what: "`${given.name}` abbreviates: ${Str.join_with(found, ", ")}" })
				}
			}
		}
		$report
	}
}

## Whether a short word stands as it is: an English word, an accepted term,
## or a letter and an axis (`dx`, `vy`).
is_plain_short_word : Str, Abbreviation.Lists -> Bool
is_plain_short_word = |w, lists| {
	if Set.contains(lists.words, w) or Set.contains(lists.accepted, w) {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		bytes = Str.to_utf8(w)
		second = List.get(bytes, 1) ?? 0
		List.len(bytes) == 2 and (second == 120 or second == 121 or second == 122)
	}
}

## Whether a word of two to four letters is short for another.
is_short_abbreviation : Str, Abbreviation.Lists -> Bool
is_short_abbreviation = |w, lists| {
	bytes = Str.to_utf8(w)
	n = List.len(bytes)
	if n < 2 or n > 4 or !(List.all(bytes, Text.is_small_letter)) {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		!(is_plain_short_word(w, lists))
	}
}

## The stems a word may be the plural of (`shapes`: `shape`, `shap`; `tries`:
## `trie`, `tri`, `try`), none for a word ending as no plural does.
plural_stems : Str -> List(Str)
plural_stems = |w| {
	n = w.count_utf8_bytes()
	no_plural = ["ss", "us", "is", "as", "os"].any(|e| Str.ends_with(w, e))
	if n < 3 or !(Str.ends_with(w, "s")) or no_plural {
		return []
	}
	one = [Text.bytes_of(w, { start: 0, count: n - 1 })]
	two = if Str.ends_with(w, "es") and n > 3 {
		one.append(Text.bytes_of(w, { start: 0, count: n - 2 }))
	} else {
		one
	}
	if Str.ends_with(w, "ies") and n > 4 {
		two.append("${Text.bytes_of(w, { start: 0, count: n - 3 })}y")
	} else {
		two
	}
}

## Whether a stem is a whole word, so its plural is plain.
is_whole_stem : Str, Abbreviation.Lists -> Bool
is_whole_stem = |stem, lists|
	if Set.contains(lists.accepted, stem) {
		Bool.True
	} else if stem.count_utf8_bytes() <= 4 {
		is_plain_short_word(stem, lists)
	} else {
		!(Set.contains(lists.abbreviations, stem))
	}

## Whether a word of a name is an abbreviation (the launcher's header says
## the rule).
is_abbreviated : Str, Abbreviation.Lists -> Bool
is_abbreviated = |word, lists| {
	letters = Str.to_utf8(word).keep_if(|b| Text.is_small_letter(b) or Text.is_digit(b))
	whole = Str.from_utf8_lossy(letters)
	if Set.contains(lists.accepted, whole) {
		return Bool.False
	}
	if Set.contains(lists.abbreviations, whole) {
		return Bool.True
	}
	var $end = List.len(letters)
	while $end > 0 and Text.is_digit(List.get(letters, $end - 1) ?? 0) {
		$end = $end - 1
	}
	w = Str.from_utf8_lossy(List.take_first(letters, $end))
	if Set.contains(lists.accepted, w) {
		return Bool.False
	}
	if Set.contains(lists.abbreviations, w) {
		return Bool.True
	}
	if w.count_utf8_bytes() <= 4 and is_plain_short_word(w, lists) {
		return Bool.False
	}
	stems = plural_stems(w)
	if stems.any(|stem| is_whole_stem(stem, lists)) {
		Bool.False
	} else if stems.any(|stem| Set.contains(lists.abbreviations, stem) or is_short_abbreviation(stem, lists)) {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		is_short_abbreviation(w, lists)
	}
}

## The tag a node names, `""` for none: a tag in a union, a pattern or an
## expression, a module's qualified tag by its last part.
tag_named : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Str
tag_named = |tree, at| {
	n = Tree.node_at(tree, at)
	if n.kind == "p-tag" or n.kind == "e-tag" {
		return Tree.last_part(Tree.attribute(n, "raw"))
	}
	if n.kind != "ty" or n.parent == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	holder = Tree.node_at(tree, n.parent)
	if holder.kind == "tags" {
		Tree.attribute(n, "name")
	} else if holder.kind == "ty-apply" and List.first(holder.kids) == Ok(at) and Tree.node_at(tree, holder.parent).kind == "tags" {
		Tree.attribute(n, "name")
	} else {
		""
	}
}

## The names a file gives or says, with the line each appears on: the
## module's, what it declares in file order, then its parameters, locals and
## tags.
names_given : Str, List(Tree.Node), Declarations -> List({ name : Str, line : U64 })
names_given = |path, tree, declared| {
	var $out = if Tree.is_app(tree) {
		[]
	} else {
		[{ name: Tree.module_name(path), line: 1 }]
	}
	for d in declared_in_file_order(declared) {
		$out = $out.append({ name: d.name, line: d.line })
	}
	var $i = 0
	for n in tree {
		$i = $i + 1
		if n.kind == "p-ident" {
			$out = $out.append({ name: Tree.attribute(n, "raw"), line: n.line })
		}
		tag = tag_named(tree, $i)
		if tag != "" and tag != "Ok" and tag != "Err" {
			$out = $out.append({ name: tag, line: n.line })
		}
	}
	$out
}

## What the file declares, its types, fields and values together, in file
## order: by the place of each one's node.
declared_in_file_order : Declarations -> List({ place : U64, name : Str, line : U64 })
declared_in_file_order = |declared| {
	types = declared.types.map(|d| { place: d.place, name: d.name, line: d.line })
	fields = declared.fields.map(|d| { place: d.place, name: d.name, line: d.line })
	values = declared.values.map(|d| { place: d.place, name: d.name, line: d.line })
	types.concat(fields).concat(values).sort_with(
		|first, second|
			if first.place < second.place {
				Before
			} else if first.place > second.place {
				After
			} else {
				Same
			},
	)
}

cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names/ModuleDoc.roc, 156 lines

## The `module_doc` check: a module with no `##` doc, or a top comment or a
## doc above its type that tells history (the launcher's header says the
## rule). A package's or platform's main.roc says which modules it keeps to
## itself, so it reads files through the platform.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

ModuleDoc := [].{

	## The findings of the file at `path`, none for an app.
	judge! : Str, List(Tree.Node), Declarations, List(Str) => List(Finding)
	judge! = |path, tree, declared, src| {
		if Tree.is_app(tree) {
			return []
		}
		name = Tree.module_name(path)
		type_line = List.fold(
			declared.types,
			0,
			|at, d| if d.name == name and d.owner == "" {
				d.line
			} else {
				at
			},
		)
		if type_line == 0 {
			return []
		}
		top = opening_comment(src)
		above_type = if type_line > 1 {
			Str.trim(Text.line_at(src, type_line - 1))
		} else {
			""
		}
		opens_with_doc = Str.starts_with(List.first(top) ?? "", "##")
		has_doc = opens_with_doc or (type_line > 1 and Str.starts_with(above_type, "##"))
		kept_to_itself = (
			!(List.is_empty(top)) or Str.starts_with(
				Str.trim(
					Text.line_at(
						src,
						if type_line > 1 {
							type_line - 1
						} else {
							1
						},
					),
				),
				"#",
			)
		) and is_private_module!(path)
		var $report = []
		if !(has_doc) and !(kept_to_itself) {
			$report = $report.append({ path, line: 1, check: "module_doc", what: "`${name}` has no `##` doc saying what it is for" })
		}
		history = history_word!(top)
		if history != "" {
			$report = $report.append({ path, line: 1, check: "module_doc", what: "`${name}`'s top comment says `${history}`: say what the module does, and leave history to git" })
		}
		doc = comment_above(src, type_line)
		doc_history = history_word!(doc.lines)
		if doc.first > 1 and doc_history != "" {
			$report = $report.append({ path, line: doc.first, check: "module_doc", what: "`${name}`'s doc says `${doc_history}`: say what the module does, and leave history to git" })
		}
		$report
	}
}

## The history word in the comment lines, or `""`. Each line's leading `#`s
## go before the lines are joined, so a phrase wrapped across two lines reads
## as one.
history_word! : List(Str) => Str
history_word! = |comment| {
	var $words = []
	for l in comment {
		$words = $words.append(Str.trim(Shale.re_replace!(l, "^#+", "")))
	}
	match Shale.re_find!(Str.with_ascii_lowercased(Str.join_with($words, " ")), "\\b(originally|used to|emitted|ported)\\b") {
		Found(m) => List.first(m.groups) ?? ""
		NoMatch => ""
	}
}

## The comment lines just above line `at`, trimmed, and the line they start
## on (`at` when there are none).
comment_above : List(Str), U64 -> { lines : List(Str), first : U64 }
comment_above = |src, at| {
	var $first = at
	while $first > 1 and Str.starts_with(Str.trim(Text.line_at(src, $first - 1)), "#") {
		$first = $first - 1
	}
	{ lines: List.sublist(src, { start: $first - 1, len: at - $first }).map(Str.trim), first: $first }
}

## The comment lines that open a file, trimmed.
opening_comment : List(Str) -> List(Str)
opening_comment = |src| {
	var $out = []
	var $going = Bool.True
	for l in src {
		if $going and Str.starts_with(Str.trim(l), "#") {
			$out = $out.append(Str.trim(l))
		} else {
			$going = Bool.False
		}
	}
	$out
}

## A file's text with its comment lines left out.
code_of : Str -> Str
code_of = |text| Str.join_with(Text.lines(text).keep_if(|l| !(Str.starts_with(Str.trim(l), "#"))), "\n")

## The names in the list between `[` and `]` of `text`.
bracketed_names : Str -> List(Str)
bracketed_names = |text|
	Str.split_on(Text.between(text, "[", "]") ?? "", ",").map(Str.trim).keep_if(|m| m != "")

## What a folder's `main.roc` exposes, when it is a package's or a
## platform's (cookbook/roc/headers.shale's `exposed_by_folder`).
exposed_by_folder! : Str => { is_package : Bool, modules : List(Str) }
exposed_by_folder! = |dir| {
	main = if dir == "" or dir == "." {
		"main.roc"
	} else {
		"${dir}/main.roc"
	}
	none = { is_package: Bool.False, modules: [] }
	match Shale.read!(main) {
		Missing => none
		Found(whole) => {
			text = code_of(whole)
			word = match Shale.re_find!(text, "[A-Za-z_]+") {
				Found(m) => m.text
				NoMatch => ""
			}
			if word == "package" {
				{ is_package: Bool.True, modules: bracketed_names(text) }
			} else if word == "platform" {
				{ is_package: Bool.True, modules: bracketed_names("${Text.between(text, "exposes", "]") ?? ""}]") }
			} else {
				none
			}
		}
	}
}

## Whether a file is a module its package keeps to itself.
is_private_module! : Str => Bool
is_private_module! = |path| {
	exposed = exposed_by_folder!(Text.dirname(path))
	exposed.is_package and !(List.contains(exposed.modules, Tree.module_name(path))) and Text.basename(path) != "main.roc"
}

## The `pure_mutator` check: an annotated pure function whose first word
## says it changes something though nothing is being added to (the
## launcher's header says the rule).
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

PureMutator := [].{

	## The finding for value `d` of the file at `path`, if it is one.
	## `aliases` are the file's structural type aliases, by name, and `terms`
	## the project's fixed terms that only look like a verb.
	judge : Str, Declarations.ValueDeclared, Dict(Str, Str), Set(Str) -> List(Finding)
	judge = |path, d, aliases, terms| {
		if !(d.is_function) or !(d.annotated) or Str.ends_with(d.name, "!") or opens_with_term(d.name, terms) {
			return []
		}
		first_word = Text.before_first(d.name, "_")
		is_mutation = is_mutation_word(first_word) and !(gives_first_back(d, aliases))
		if first_word == "get" or is_mutation {
			[{ path, line: d.line, check: "pure_mutator", what: "`${d.name}` is pure and gives a new `${d.result_type}`: name it for what it gives" }]
		} else {
			[]
		}
	}
}

## The value of a `Try(value, errors)`, or `result` when it is no `Try`.
value_of_try : Str -> Str
value_of_try = |result| {
	if !(Str.starts_with(result, "Try(")) {
		return result
	}
	bytes = Str.to_utf8(result)
	var $depth = 0
	var $k = 4
	while $k < List.len(bytes) {
		b = List.get(bytes, $k) ?? 0
		if b == 40 or b == 123 or b == 91 {
			$depth = $depth + 1
		} else if b == 41 or b == 125 or b == 93 {
			if $depth == 0 {
				return result
			}
			$depth = $depth - 1
		} else if b == 44 and $depth == 0 {
			return Str.trim(Text.bytes_of(result, { start: 4, count: $k - 4 }))
		}
		$k = $k + 1
	}
	result
}

record_holds : Str, Str -> Bool
record_holds = |record, type_name|
	Str.starts_with(record, "{") and (Str.contains(record, " : ${type_name},") or Str.contains(record, " : ${type_name} }"))

## Whether a function's result is what its first argument was added to.
gives_first_back : Declarations.ValueDeclared, Dict(Str, Str) -> Bool
gives_first_back = |d, aliases| {
	value = value_of_try(d.result_type)
	if value == d.first_type or record_holds(d.first_type, value) {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		record_holds(Dict.get(aliases, Tree.last_part(value)) ?? value, d.first_type)
	}
}

opens_with_term : Str, Set(Str) -> Bool
opens_with_term = |name, terms| Set.to_list(terms).any(|term| name == term or Str.starts_with(name, "${term}_"))

is_mutation_word : Str -> Bool
is_mutation_word = |w| w == "push" or w == "fill" or w == "set" or w == "append" or w == "add"

## The recipe's self-test: each plant under
## cookbook/roc/plants/find_unclear_names/ run through the launcher, held to
## its findings, its exit and what it says (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `check_plants`).
import pf.Shale
import lib.Text

SelfTest := [].{

	## Each row run as a child of its own, through `launcher`; a check of
	## `checks` no row fires fails too, since it could be blind.
	run! : List(Str) => {}
	run! = |checks| {
		var $wrong = 0
		var $fired = Set.empty()
		for row in rows {
			argv = List.concat(["shale", launcher, "glob=${row.glob}"], row.args)
			r = Shale.run!({ argv, keep: Whole(4000000), timeout_ms: 120000, want: "" })
			faults = row_faults!(row, r, checks)
			for pair in row.counts {
				$fired = Set.insert($fired, pair.0)
			}
			if List.is_empty(faults) {
				Shale.print!("ok   ${row.glob}")
			} else {
				Shale.print!("FAIL ${row.glob}: ${Str.join_with(faults, "; ")}")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
				Shale.print!(r.out)
			}
		}
		for check in checks {
			if !(Set.contains($fired, check)) {
				Shale.print!("FAIL `${check}` has no plant")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
			}
		}
		if $wrong > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("find_unclear_names self_test: ${U64.to_str($wrong)} wrong")
		}
		Shale.print!("find_unclear_names self_test: PASS (${U64.to_str(List.len(rows))} rows: each plant gives its findings and a nonzero exit, each clean case none and exit 0)")
	}
}

## The launcher, which the self-test runs each plant through.
launcher : Str
launcher = "cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale"

Row : { glob : Str, args : List(Str), counts : List((Str, U64)), says : List(Str), stops : Bool }

plants : Str
plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_unclear_names/"

clean : Str -> Row
clean = |glob| { glob: "${plants}${glob}", args: [], counts: [], says: [], stops: Bool.False }

fires : Str, List(Str), List((Str, U64)), List(Str) -> Row
fires = |glob, args, counts, says| { glob: "${plants}${glob}", args, counts, says, stops: Bool.False }

stops : Str, List(Str), List(Str) -> Row
stops = |glob, args, says| { glob: "${plants}${glob}", args, counts: [], says, stops: Bool.True }

rows : List(Row)
rows = [
	fires("pure_mutator.roc", [], [("pure_mutator", 7)], ["pure_mutator.roc:3: pure_mutator: `push_cat` is pure and gives a new `List(U64)`", "`get_speed`"]),
	clean("quiet_pure_mutator.roc"),
	fires("terms.roc", [], [("pure_mutator", 2)], ["`set_cookie_header`", "`set_cookies`"]),
	fires("terms.roc", ["terms=${plants}terms.txt"], [("pure_mutator", 1)], ["`set_cookies`"]),
	stops("terms.roc", ["terms=${plants}no_such.txt"], ["no word list"]),
	fires("abbreviation.roc", [], [("abbreviation", 4)], ["abbreviation.roc:3: abbreviation: `max_vis_cats` abbreviates: vis", "`SunPos` abbreviates: pos", "`dist` abbreviates: dist"]),
	clean("quiet_abbreviation.roc"),
	fires("abbreviation.roc", ["abbreviations=${plants}project_words.txt"], [("abbreviation", 4)], ["`max_vis_cats` abbreviates: vis, cats"]),
	fires("short_words/*.roc", [], [("abbreviation", 5)], ["Tbl.roc:1: abbreviation: `Tbl` abbreviates: tbl", "Tbl.roc:4: abbreviation: `Trk` abbreviates: trk", "Tbl.roc:7: abbreviation: `trk` abbreviates: trk", "`pts` abbreviates: pts", "Tbl.roc:9: abbreviation: `hgt` abbreviates: hgt"]),
	clean("quiet_short_words/*.roc"),
	fires("short_words/*.roc", ["accepted=${plants}project_terms.txt"], [("abbreviation", 3)], ["`Tbl` abbreviates: tbl", "`pts` abbreviates: pts", "`hgt` abbreviates: hgt"]),
	{ ..clean("quiet_short_words/*.roc"), args: ["accepted=${plants}project_terms.txt"] },
	stops("quiet_short_words/*.roc", ["accepted=${plants}no_reason.txt"], ["`qty` has no reason"]),
	stops("quiet_abbreviation.roc", ["abbreviations=${plants}no_such.txt"], ["no word list"]),
	fires("long_abbreviations/*.roc", [], [("abbreviation", 11)], ["Parser.roc:5: abbreviation: `attrs` abbreviates: attrs", "`idxes` abbreviates: idxes", "`vals` abbreviates: vals", "`delim` abbreviates: delim", "`parse_args` abbreviates: args", "`params` abbreviates: params", "`elem_count` abbreviates: elem", "`expr_text` abbreviates: expr", "`stmt_kind` abbreviates: stmt", "`tmpl_name` abbreviates: tmpl"]),
	fires("long_abbreviations/*.roc", ["accepted=${plants}project_args.txt"], [("abbreviation", 9)], ["`attrs` abbreviates: attrs", "`params` abbreviates: params"]),
	clean("quiet_long_abbreviations/*.roc"),
	fires("common_words/*.roc", [], [("abbreviation", 2)], ["`Flw` abbreviates: flw", "`night_dmr` abbreviates: dmr"]),
	clean("quiet_common_words/*.roc"),
	fires("tags.roc", [], [("abbreviation", 5)], ["tags.roc:14: abbreviation: `TmplGone` abbreviates: tmpl", "tags.roc:4: abbreviation: `NoRef` abbreviates: ref", "tags.roc:4: abbreviation: `Ref` abbreviates: ref", "tags.roc:6: abbreviation: `TmplMissing` abbreviates: tmpl", "tags.roc:12: abbreviation: `BadAttr` abbreviates: attr"]),
	clean("quiet_tags.roc"),
	fires("module_doc/*.roc", [], [("module_doc", 5)], ["`NoDoc` has no `##` doc", "`Hashless` has no `##` doc", "`Old`'s top comment says `originally`", "`Sky`'s top comment says `used to`", "Sun.roc:3: module_doc: `Sun`'s doc says `originally`"]),
	clean("quiet_module_doc/*.roc"),
	fires("module_doc_private/*.roc", [], [("module_doc", 2)], ["`Shown` has no `##` doc", "`Silent` has no `##` doc"]),
	stops("broken/*.roc", [], ["refused: "]),
]

## The last line of `out` that isn't one of Shale's `──` lines.
last_said : Str -> Str
last_said = |out| List.fold(
	Text.lines(Str.trim(out)),
	"",
	|last, l| if Str.starts_with(l, "──") or Str.trim(l) == "" {
		last
	} else {
		l
	},
)

## What is wrong with one row's run (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `row_faults`).
row_faults! : Row, { code : I64, out : Str }, List(Str) => List(Str)
row_faults! = |row, r, checks| {
	must_fail = row.stops or !(List.is_empty(row.counts))
	var $faults = []
	if must_fail and r.code == 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited 0")
	}
	if !(must_fail) and r.code != 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited ${I64.to_str(r.code)}")
	}
	for check in checks {
		found = List.len(Shale.re_lines!(r.out, "^[^ ]+:[0-9]+: ${check}: "))
		wanted = List.fold(
			row.counts,
			0,
			|n, pair| if pair.0 == check {
				pair.1
			} else {
				n
			},
		)
		if found != wanted {
			$faults = $faults.append("${check} printed ${U64.to_str(found)}, not ${U64.to_str(wanted)}")
		}
	}
	if !(row.stops) and !(Str.contains(last_said(r.out), " files; ")) {
		$faults = $faults.append("its last line is no summary: ${last_said(r.out)}")
	}
	for literal in row.says {
		if !(Str.contains(r.out, literal)) {
			$faults = $faults.append("its output lacks `${literal}`")
		}
	}
	$faults
}

-- This recipe finds names and top comments that say less than they should: a
-- pure function named like a mutation, an abbreviation in a name, and a
-- module with no doc or with history where its doc belongs.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_unclear_names.shale
--   shale cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob           the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default;
--   abbreviations  the file of abbreviations, one a line, by default
--                  cookbook/words/abbreviations.txt, for a project with
--                  words of its own to add;
--   words          the English words of two to four letters a name may hold,
--                  by default cookbook/words/short_words.txt;
--   accepted       a project's file of the short terms a name may hold though
--                  they are no English word, each with its reason, added to
--                  cookbook/words/accepted_terms.txt (`html`, `url`, `utf8`);
--   terms          a project's file of fixed terms that open a name and only
--                  look like a verb, one a line, such as `set_cookie` for
--                  HTTP's header, which `pure_mutator` leaves alone;
--   house          with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style
--                  (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code;
--   self_test      with `self_test=1`, check the plants in
--                  `cookbook/roc/plants/find_unclear_names/`.
--
-- The checks read top-level names, module members and the record fields of
-- types and annotations; `abbreviation` reads module names, parameters,
-- locals and tags too:
--
--   pure_mutator  An annotated pure function whose first word says it changes
--                 something (`push`, `fill`, `set`, `append`, `add`), though
--                 nothing is being added to. Something is when the result is
--                 the first argument's type, on its own, as a `Try`'s value,
--                 or as a field of a record or of an alias in the same file
--                 (`Try({ users : Users, user : User }, [Full])`), or when the
--                 first argument is a record with a field of the result's
--                 type (`{ so_far : List(U8), count : U64 }`). A first word
--                 `get` always counts, because a Roc function's plain name
--                 is already what it gets.
--   abbreviation  A name with a word short for another, since Roc's style
--                 guide prefers the plain word: a word from the
--                 abbreviations file, whatever its length (`delim`,
--                 `param`, `args`), the plural of an abbreviation (`attrs`,
--                 `params`), or a word of two to four letters (`st`, `tks`,
--                 `Inl`, `Emph`) that is no English word of the words file,
--                 no accepted term, no plural of either, and no letter and
--                 an axis (`dx`). A term accepted, the cookbook's or the
--                 project's, is never one, even one the abbreviations file
--                 lists (a project's `args`). A word ending as no plural
--                 does (`class`, `bonus`, `alias`) is no plural. A type's words are split at
--                 its capitals, so `TkKind` holds `tk`. A word's marks and
--                 trailing digits go first (`buf0` is `buf`), and a letter
--                 alone is hunt_names' `short_name`'s. The names read are a
--                 module's own (its file's), every type, member, field and
--                 top-level value, every parameter and local, and every tag
--                 in a union, a pattern or an expression, split at its
--                 capitals as a type is (`NoRef` holds `ref`), but Roc's own
--                 `Ok` and `Err`. A name is reported once a file.
--   module_doc    A module with no `##` doc at the top of its file or above
--                 its type, or a top comment or a doc above its type that
--                 tells history (`originally`, `used to`, `emitted`,
--                 `ported`, even wrapped across two lines) instead of what
--                 the module does. A
--                 module its package or platform keeps to itself has no public
--                 doc to write, so any comment there will do. App files are
--                 left out, as they have no module type.
--
-- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again
-- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if
-- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way.
-- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const ABBREVIATIONS_FILE = arg("abbreviations", "cookbook:words/abbreviations.txt")
const SHORT_WORDS_FILE = arg("words", "cookbook:words/short_words.txt")
const ACCEPTED_FILE = "cookbook:words/accepted_terms.txt"
const PROJECT_ACCEPTED_FILE = arg("accepted", "")
const TERMS_FILE = arg("terms", "")
use("./declared.shale")
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./gate_recipe.shale")
use("./headers.shale")
use("./house.shale")
const CHECKS = {"pure_mutator", "abbreviation", "module_doc"}
const MUTATION_WORDS = {push = true, fill = true, set = true, append = true, add = true}
const HISTORY_RE = "\\b(originally|used to|emitted|ported)\\b"

-- The value of a `Try(value, errors)`, or `result` when it is no `Try`.
function value_of_try(result)
  if not starts_with(result, "Try(") then return result end
  local depth = 0
  for i = 5, #result do
    local c = sub(result, i, i)
    if c == "(" or c == "{" or c == "[" then
      depth = depth + 1
    elseif c == ")" or c == "}" or c == "]" then
      depth = depth - 1
    elseif c == "," and depth == 0 then
      return trim(sub(result, 5, i - 1))
    end
  end
  return result
end

function record_holds(record, type_name)
  return starts_with(record, "{") and (contains(record, " : " .. type_name .. ",") or contains(record, " : " .. type_name .. " }"))
end

-- Whether a function's result is what its first argument was added to.
function gives_first_back(d, aliases)
  local value = value_of_try(d.result)
  if value == d.first or record_holds(d.first, value) then return true end
  return record_holds(get(aliases, last_part(value), value), d.first)
end

function opens_with_term(name, terms)
  for term in keys(terms) do
    if name == term or starts_with(name, term .. "_") then return true end
  end
  return false
end

function judge_mutator(d, aliases, terms, report)
  if not d.fn or not d.annotated or ends_with(d.name, "!") or opens_with_term(d.name, terms) then return nil end
  local first_word = split(d.name, "_")[1]
  local is_mutation = has_key(MUTATION_WORDS, first_word) and not gives_first_back(d, aliases)
  if first_word == "get" or is_mutation then
    push(report, {path = d.path, line = d.line, check = "pure_mutator", what = "`" .. d.name .. "` is pure and gives a new `" .. d.result .. "`: name it for what it gives"})
  end
  return nil
end

-- The accepted terms file: a term a line, each with its reason after `--`,
-- as a set. A line without a reason fails the run.
function accepted_terms(path)
  if not exists(path) then fail("no word list " .. path) end
  for l in lines(read(path)) do
    local term = trim(split(l, "--")[1])
    if term ~= "" and trim(get(split(l, "--"), 2, "")) == "" then fail(path .. ": `" .. term .. "` has no reason after `--`") end
  end
  return word_set(path)
end

-- Whether a short word stands as it is: an English word, an accepted term,
-- or a letter and an axis (`dx`, `vy`), a coordinate's change or part.
function is_plain_short_word(w, lists)
  if has_key(lists.words, w) or has_key(lists.accepted, w) then return true end
  return #w == 2 and has_item({"x", "y", "z"}, sub(w, 2, 2))
end

-- Whether a word of two to four letters is short for another: no plain
-- short word.
function is_short_abbreviation(w, lists)
  if #w < 2 or #w > 4 or re_find(w, "^[a-z]+$") == nil then return false end
  return not is_plain_short_word(w, lists)
end

-- The stems a word may be the plural of, each way English makes one:
-- `shapes` gives `shape` and `shap`, `boxes` `boxe` and `box`, and `tries`
-- `trie`, `tri` and `try`. None for a word that ends as no plural does
-- (`class`, `bonus`, `alias`, `basis`, `chaos`).
function plural_stems(w)
  if #w < 3 or not ends_with(w, "s") or re_find(w, "(ss|us|is|as|os)$") ~= nil then return {} end
  local stems = {sub(w, 1, #w - 1)}
  if ends_with(w, "es") and #w > 3 then push(stems, sub(w, 1, #w - 2)) end
  if ends_with(w, "ies") and #w > 4 then push(stems, sub(w, 1, #w - 3) .. "y") end
  return stems
end

-- Whether a stem is a whole word, so its plural is plain: an accepted term,
-- a plain short word, or a stem past four letters that the abbreviations
-- file doesn't list, since only a word of two to four letters is judged
-- by its length (`shape` of `shapes`, `frame` of `frames`).
function is_whole_stem(stem, lists)
  if has_key(lists.accepted, stem) then return true end
  if #stem <= 4 then return is_plain_short_word(stem, lists) end
  return not has_key(lists.abbreviations, stem)
end

-- Whether a word of a name is an abbreviation. A term the cookbook or the
-- project accepts never is, and one the abbreviations file lists always is,
-- whatever its length (`delim`, `params`). A plural is judged by every
-- stem it could have (`plural_stems`): it is plain when any stem is a whole
-- word (`ids`, `boxes`, `shapes`, `tries`), and else an abbreviation when a
-- stem is one (`attrs`, `delims`). Past those, a word of two to four
-- letters that is no plain word is one. Its marks (`!`, `$`) and trailing
-- digits (`buf0`) go first; a letter alone is `short_name`'s, in hunt_names.
function is_abbreviated(word, lists)
  local w = re_replace(word, "[^a-z0-9]", "")
  if has_key(lists.accepted, w) then return false end
  if has_key(lists.abbreviations, w) then return true end
  w = re_replace(w, "[0-9]+$", "")
  if has_key(lists.accepted, w) then return false end
  if has_key(lists.abbreviations, w) then return true end
  if #w <= 4 and is_plain_short_word(w, lists) then return false end
  local stems = plural_stems(w)
  for stem in stems do
    if is_whole_stem(stem, lists) then return false end
  end
  for stem in stems do
    if has_key(lists.abbreviations, stem) or is_short_abbreviation(stem, lists) then return true end
  end
  return is_short_abbreviation(w, lists)
end

-- Roc's own tags, which every file may say and none names.
const ROC_TAGS = {Ok = true, Err = true}

-- The tag a node names, `""` for none: a tag in a union (`[NoRef, Ref(Str)]`,
-- the bare one and the head of the one with a payload), in a pattern and in
-- an expression. A tag a module qualifies (`Bool.False`, which a pattern's
-- tree gives as `.False`) is its last part alone: the module's name is
-- judged in the module's own file, and a builtin's (`Bool`) is Roc's.
function tag_named(tree, at)
  local n = tree[at]
  if n.kind == "p-tag" or n.kind == "e-tag" then
    local parts = split(get(n, "raw", ""), ".")
    return parts[#parts]
  end
  if n.kind ~= "ty" or n.parent == 0 then return "" end
  local holder = tree[n.parent]
  if holder.kind == "tags" then return get(n, "name", "") end
  if holder.kind == "ty-apply" and holder.kids[1] == at and tree[holder.parent].kind == "tags" then return get(n, "name", "") end
  return ""
end

-- The names a file gives or says, each once, with the line it first appears
-- on: its module's name, what it declares, each parameter and local, and
-- each tag but Roc's own (ROC_TAGS), split at its capitals as a type is.
function names_given(f, declared)
  local out = {}
  if not is_app(f) then push(out, {name = module_name(f.path), line = 1}) end
  for d in declared do push(out, {name = d.name, line = d.line}) end
  for i = 1, #f.nodes do
    local n = f.nodes[i]
    if n.kind == "p-ident" then push(out, {name = get(n, "raw", ""), line = n.line}) end
    local tag = tag_named(f.nodes, i)
    if tag ~= "" and not has_key(ROC_TAGS, tag) then push(out, {name = tag, line = n.line}) end
  end
  return out
end

function judge_abbreviations(f, declared, lists, report)
  local seen = {}
  for given in names_given(f, declared) do
    if not has_key(seen, given.name) then
      seen[given.name] = true
      local found = {}
      for w in name_words(given.name) do
        if is_abbreviated(w, lists) then push(found, w) end
      end
      if #found > 0 then push(report, {path = f.path, line = given.line, check = "abbreviation", what = "`" .. given.name .. "` abbreviates: " .. join(found, ", ")}) end
    end
  end
  return nil
end

-- The history word in the comment lines `comment`, or nil. Each line's
-- leading `#`s go before the lines are joined, so a phrase wrapped across
-- two lines reads as one.
function history_word(comment)
  local words = {}
  for l in comment do push(words, trim(re_replace(l, "^#+", ""))) end
  local found = re_find(lower(join(words, " ")), HISTORY_RE)
  if found == nil then return nil end
  return found.group
end

-- The comment lines just above line `at` of `src`, trimmed, as `{lines,
-- first}`, where `first` is the line the comment starts on, or `at` when
-- there is none.
function comment_above(src, at)
  local first = at
  while first > 1 and starts_with(trim(src[first - 1]), "#") do first = first - 1 end
  local out = {}
  for k = first, at - 1 do push(out, trim(src[k])) end
  return {lines = out, first = first}
end

function judge_module_doc(f, declared, report)
  if is_app(f) then return nil end
  local name = module_name(f.path)
  local type_line = 0
  for d in declared do
    if d.kind == "type" and d.name == name and d.owner == "" then type_line = d.line end
  end
  if type_line == 0 then return nil end
  local src = split(read(f.path), "\n")
  local top = opening_comment(src)
  local has_doc = (#top > 0 and starts_with(top[1], "##")) or (type_line > 1 and starts_with(trim(src[type_line - 1]), "##"))
  if is_private_module(f.path) and (#top > 0 or starts_with(trim(src[max(type_line - 1, 1)]), "#")) then has_doc = true end
  if not has_doc then push(report, {path = f.path, line = 1, check = "module_doc", what = "`" .. name .. "` has no `##` doc saying what it is for"}) end
  local history = history_word(top)
  if history ~= nil then push(report, {path = f.path, line = 1, check = "module_doc", what = "`" .. name .. "`'s top comment says `" .. history .. "`: say what the module does, and leave history to git"}) end
  local doc = comment_above(src, type_line)
  local doc_history = history_word(doc.lines)
  if doc.first > 1 and doc_history ~= nil then
    push(report, {path = f.path, line = doc.first, check = "module_doc", what = "`" .. name .. "`'s doc says `" .. doc_history .. "`: say what the module does, and leave history to git"})
  end
  return nil
end

function self_test()
  local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_unclear_names/"
  check_plants("find_unclear_names", "cookbook:roc/find_unclear_names.shale", CHECKS, {
    {glob = at .. "pure_mutator.roc", counts = {pure_mutator = 7}, says = {"pure_mutator.roc:3: pure_mutator: `push_cat` is pure and gives a new `List(U64)`", "`get_speed`"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_pure_mutator.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "terms.roc", counts = {pure_mutator = 2}, says = {"`set_cookie_header`", "`set_cookies`"}},
    {glob = at .. "terms.roc", args = {"terms=" .. at .. "terms.txt"}, counts = {pure_mutator = 1}, says = {"`set_cookies`"}},
    {glob = at .. "terms.roc", args = {"terms=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no word list"}},
    {glob = at .. "abbreviation.roc", counts = {abbreviation = 4}, says = {"abbreviation.roc:3: abbreviation: `max_vis_cats` abbreviates: vis", "`SunPos` abbreviates: pos", "`dist` abbreviates: dist"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_abbreviation.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "abbreviation.roc", args = {"abbreviations=" .. at .. "project_words.txt"}, counts = {abbreviation = 4}, says = {"`max_vis_cats` abbreviates: vis, cats"}},
    {glob = at .. "short_words/*.roc", counts = {abbreviation = 5}, says = {"Tbl.roc:1: abbreviation: `Tbl` abbreviates: tbl", "Tbl.roc:4: abbreviation: `Trk` abbreviates: trk", "Tbl.roc:7: abbreviation: `trk` abbreviates: trk", "`pts` abbreviates: pts", "Tbl.roc:9: abbreviation: `hgt` abbreviates: hgt"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_short_words/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "short_words/*.roc", args = {"accepted=" .. at .. "project_terms.txt"}, counts = {abbreviation = 3}, says = {"`Tbl` abbreviates: tbl", "`pts` abbreviates: pts", "`hgt` abbreviates: hgt"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_short_words/*.roc", args = {"accepted=" .. at .. "project_terms.txt"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_short_words/*.roc", args = {"accepted=" .. at .. "no_reason.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"`qty` has no reason"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_abbreviation.roc", args = {"abbreviations=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no word list"}},
    {glob = at .. "long_abbreviations/*.roc", counts = {abbreviation = 11}, says = {"Parser.roc:5: abbreviation: `attrs` abbreviates: attrs", "`idxes` abbreviates: idxes", "`vals` abbreviates: vals", "`delim` abbreviates: delim", "`parse_args` abbreviates: args", "`params` abbreviates: params", "`elem_count` abbreviates: elem", "`expr_text` abbreviates: expr", "`stmt_kind` abbreviates: stmt", "`tmpl_name` abbreviates: tmpl"}},
    {glob = at .. "long_abbreviations/*.roc", args = {"accepted=" .. at .. "project_args.txt"}, counts = {abbreviation = 9}, says = {"`attrs` abbreviates: attrs", "`params` abbreviates: params"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_long_abbreviations/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "common_words/*.roc", counts = {abbreviation = 2}, says = {"`Flw` abbreviates: flw", "`night_dmr` abbreviates: dmr"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_common_words/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "tags.roc", counts = {abbreviation = 5}, says = {"tags.roc:14: abbreviation: `TmplGone` abbreviates: tmpl", "tags.roc:4: abbreviation: `NoRef` abbreviates: ref", "tags.roc:4: abbreviation: `Ref` abbreviates: ref", "tags.roc:6: abbreviation: `TmplMissing` abbreviates: tmpl", "tags.roc:12: abbreviation: `BadAttr` abbreviates: attr"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_tags.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "module_doc/*.roc", counts = {module_doc = 5}, says = {"`NoDoc` has no `##` doc", "`Hashless` has no `##` doc", "`Old`'s top comment says `originally`", "`Sky`'s top comment says `used to`", "Sun.roc:3: module_doc: `Sun`'s doc says `originally`"}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_module_doc/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "module_doc_private/*.roc", counts = {module_doc = 2}, says = {"`Shown` has no `##` doc", "`Silent` has no `##` doc"}},
    {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}},
  })
  return nil
end

function run_check()
  local lists = {abbreviations = word_set(ABBREVIATIONS_FILE), words = word_set(SHORT_WORDS_FILE), accepted = accepted_terms(ACCEPTED_FILE)}
  if PROJECT_ACCEPTED_FILE ~= "" then
    for term in keys(accepted_terms(PROJECT_ACCEPTED_FILE)) do lists.accepted[term] = true end
  end
  local terms = TERMS_FILE == "" and {} or word_set(TERMS_FILE)
  local paths = glob(GLOB)
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths)
  local report = {}
  for f in parsed.files do
    local declared = declarations_of(f)
    local aliases = {}
    for d in declared do
      if d.kind == "type" and not d.is_nominal then aliases[d.name] = d.underlying end
    end
    for d in declared do
      if d.kind == "value" then judge_mutator(d, aliases, terms, report) end
    end
    if not house_leaves_out("find_unclear_names", "abbreviation") then judge_abbreviations(f, declared, lists, report) end
    judge_module_doc(f, declared, report)
  end
  local verdict = verdict_of("find_unclear_names", CHECKS, report, #paths)
  verdict.summary = verdict.summary .. house_note("find_unclear_names")
  print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found)
  fail_if_refused("find_unclear_names", parsed.refused)
  return verdict
end

-- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a
-- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it.
if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
else
  local verdict = run_check()
  if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end
end

find_unused_imports

The import lines a Roc file never uses, read from Roc's own parse tree, a gate with its plants' self-test in Roc too.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_lines!, Shale.read!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!.
Roc: 474 lines in 3 files. Shale original: 106 lines, plus 261 lines in the 4 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Finding, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports/find_unused_imports.roc, 112 lines

## find_unused_imports, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## the import lines a Roc file never uses, since Roc doesn't warn of one. Its
## launcher, cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports.shale, is how it is run, and
## its header says the rule, `unused_import`. check_goldens.shale, beside
## this, holds its output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale glob=app/**/*.roc
##   shale cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`; several, separated by commas) and
## `self_test` (`self_test=1` runs the plants, each through the launcher).
##
## This root globs the files, has Roc's parser read them (`Shale.roc_tree!`)
## and each one's text (`Shale.read!`), and prints the verdict
## (`Shale.print!`, `Shale.fail!`). Imports, beside it, is the rule;
## SelfTest is the plants' run. Tree, Text and Finding are the cookbook's Roc
## library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 programs=100
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import Imports
import SelfTest

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	if Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1" {
		SelfTest.run!({})
	} else {
		run_check!({})
	}
}

## The check over the glob's files: the verdict printed, then a stop when a
## file didn't parse, or when there are findings, the summary the last line
## a caller reads.
run_check! : {} => {}
run_check! = |{}| {
	paths = list_files!(Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc"))
	var $report = []
	var $refused = []
	for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if file.err == "" {
			source_lines = read_text!(file.path).split_on("\n")
			for unused in Imports.unused_imports(file.nodes, source_lines) {
				what = "${unused.label} is imported and never used: delete the line"
				$report = $report.append({ path: file.path, line: unused.line, check: "unused_import", what })
			}
		} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
			$refused = $refused.append(file.err)
		} else {
			$refused = $refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}")
		}
	}
	found = $report.sort_with(Finding.order).map(Finding.line_of)
	counts = "${paths.len().to_str()} files; unused_import ${found.len().to_str()}"
	summary = "find_unused_imports (Roc): ${counts}"
	print_findings!(summary, found)
	if !($refused.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in $refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		refused_count = $refused.len().to_str()
		refusals = "roc-ast refused ${refused_count} files (named above)"
		why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
		Shale.fail!("find_unused_imports: ${refusals}, ${why}")
	}
	if !(found.is_empty()) {
		Shale.fail!(summary)
	}
}

## The files of each comma-separated glob, in the order given, a file twice
## when two globs name it.
list_files! : Str => List(Str)
list_files! = |patterns| {
	var $paths = []
	for pattern in patterns.split_on(",") {
		matching = Shale.glob!(Text.trim(pattern))
		$paths = $paths.concat(matching)
	}
	$paths
}

## The file's text. A file the parser read and the read finds gone stops the
## run.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("find_unused_imports: ${path} went missing during the check")
			""
		}
	}

# ── The verdict

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports/Imports.roc, 209 lines

## A Roc file's imports, read from Roc's own tree of it, and the ones the file
## never uses. The rules are the recipe's `unused_import`
## (cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports.shale's header says what counts as a
## use); cookbook/roc/imports.shale holds the same rules for the Shale
## recipes that ask them of a file, rewrite_method_calls.shale among them.
import lib.Tree

Imports := [].{

	## An import line no name of the file uses: its line and how a finding
	## names it.
	UnusedImport : { line : U64, label : Str }

	## Each import of the file whose names it never uses, from its tree and
	## its source lines, which hold the qualifier of a pattern's tag that the
	## tree drops.
	unused_imports : List(Tree.Node), List(Str) -> List(Imports.UnusedImport)
	unused_imports = |nodes, source_lines| {
		used = heads_used(nodes, source_lines)
		imports_of(nodes)
			.drop_if(|line_import| line_import.names.any(|name| used.contains(name)))
			.map(|line_import| { line: line_import.line, label: line_import.label })
	}
}

## An import line: its line, how a finding names it, and the names a use of
## it may start with.
Import : {
	line : U64,
	label : Str,
	names : List(Str),
}

## The kids of a node, as nodes.
kid_nodes : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> List(Tree.Node)
kid_nodes = |nodes, node|
	node.kids.map(|at| Tree.node_at(nodes, at))

# ── The imports

## Each import of the file, in order: `import pkg.Mod`, its alias and what it
## exposes, and each file import, `import "page.html" as page : Str`.
imports_of : List(Tree.Node) -> List(Import)
imports_of = |nodes|
	nodes.join_map(
		|node|
			if node.kind == "s-import" {
				[module_import(nodes, node)]
			} else if node.kind == "s-file-import" {
				file_imports(nodes, node)
			} else {
				[]
			},
	)

## A module's import. Its name is the alias of `import pkg.Mod as M`, else
## the last part of the module's path; a name it exposes is one too.
module_import : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> Import
module_import = |nodes, node| {
	path = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	alias = Tree.attribute(node, "alias")
	name = if alias == "" {
		path.split_on(".").last() ?? path
	} else {
		alias
	}
	label = if alias == "" {
		"`${path}`"
	} else {
		"`${path}` as `${alias}`"
	}
	exposing_lists = kid_nodes(nodes, node).keep_if(|kid| kid.kind == "exposing")
	exposed = exposing_lists.join_map(|list| exposed_names(nodes, list))
	{
		line: node.line,
		label,
		names: exposed.prepend(name),
	}
}

## The names an `exposing [...]` list names: a type's `text`, and each
## value's name, held by the value's own kids.
exposed_names : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> List(Str)
exposed_names = |nodes, list|
	kid_nodes(nodes, list).join_map(
		|entry|
			if entry.kind == "exposed-upper-ident" {
				[Tree.attribute(entry, "text")]
			} else if entry.kind == "exposed-lower-ident" {
				kid_nodes(nodes, entry).map(|name| Tree.attribute(name, "value"))
			} else {
				[]
			},
	)

## A file import's name, used when the file refers to it.
file_imports : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> List(Import)
file_imports = |nodes, node|
	kid_nodes(nodes, node)
		.keep_if(|kid| kid.kind == "name")
		.map(
			|kid| {
				name = Tree.attribute(kid, "value")
				{
					line: node.line,
					label: "the file import `${name}`",
					names: [name],
				}
			},
		)

# ── The uses

## The first part of every value, tag and type name the file uses. A bare
## tag (`Other`, in an expression, a pattern or a tag union type) names no
## module, so only a qualified one counts, or one that is a nominal type's
## name (`Point.{ x: 0 }`). A platform header's `hosted { "sym": Host.f! }`
## entry uses its module.
heads_used : List(Tree.Node), List(Str) -> Set(Str)
heads_used = |nodes, source_lines| {
	union_tags = kids_of_kind(nodes, "tags")
	nominal_names = kids_of_kind(nodes, "mapper")
	names = nodes.map_with_index(
		|node, index| {
			at = index + 1
			if node.kind == "e-ident" {
				Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
			} else if node.kind == "e-tag" {
				tag_use(node, nominal_names.contains(at))
			} else if node.kind == "ty" and !(union_tags.contains(at)) {
				Tree.attribute(node, "name")
			} else if node.kind == "symbol-map-entry" {
				Tree.attribute(node, "module")
			} else if node.kind == "p-tag" {
				pattern_tag_use(node, source_lines)
			} else {
				""
			}
		},
	)
	Set.from_list(names.drop_if(Str.is_empty).map(head_of))
}

## An expression's tag, when it names a module: qualified, or a nominal
## type's name.
tag_use : Tree.Node, Bool -> Str
tag_use = |node, names_nominal| {
	raw = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	if raw.contains(".") or names_nominal {
		raw
	} else {
		""
	}
}

## A pattern's tag, when it is qualified. roc-ast drops a pattern tag's
## qualifier (`Color.Red =>` comes as `.Red`), so the tag is read from the
## source at the pattern's column.
pattern_tag_use : Tree.Node, List(Str) -> Str
pattern_tag_use = |node, source_lines| {
	raw = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	written = if raw.starts_with(".") {
		source_line = match source_lines.get(node.line - 1) {
			Ok(text) => text
			Err(_) => crash "find_unused_imports: a pattern's tag past the file's end"
		}
		written_name(source_line.to_utf8().drop_first(node.col - 1))
	} else {
		raw
	}
	if written.contains(".") {
		written
	} else {
		""
	}
}

## The dotted name the bytes start with: a letter or `_`, then letters,
## digits, `_` and `.`; `""` when they start with none.
written_name : List(U8) -> Str
written_name = |bytes|
	match bytes.first() {
		Ok(first) if is_letter(first) or first == '_' => {
			length = bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_name_byte(byte))) ?? bytes.len()
			match Str.from_utf8(bytes.take_first(length)) {
				Ok(name) => name
				Err(_) => crash "find_unused_imports: a name of ASCII bytes is UTF-8"
			}
		}
		_ => ""
	}

is_letter : U8 -> Bool
is_letter = |byte|
	(byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z')

is_name_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_name_byte = |byte|
	is_letter(byte) or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9') or byte == '_' or byte == '.'

## The first part of a dotted name: `Mod` of `Mod.Type.name`.
head_of : Str -> Str
head_of = |name|
	name.split_on(".").first() ?? name

## The places of the nodes that are kids of a node of the kind.
kids_of_kind : List(Tree.Node), Str -> Set(U64)
kids_of_kind = |nodes, kind|
	Set.from_list(nodes.keep_if(|node| node.kind == kind).join_map(|node| node.kids))

cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports/SelfTest.roc, 153 lines

## The recipe's self-test: each plant under
## cookbook/roc/plants/find_unused_imports/ run through the launcher, held to
## its findings, its exit and what it says (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `check_plants`).
import pf.Shale

SelfTest := [].{

	## Each row run as a child of its own, through the launcher; a run that
	## fires no `unused_import` anywhere fails too, since the check could be
	## blind.
	run! : {} => {}
	run! = |{}| {
		var $wrong = 0
		for row in rows {
			pattern = "${plants}${row.plant}"
			command = ["shale", launcher, "glob=${pattern}"]
			result = Shale.run!({
				argv: command,
				keep: Whole(4000000),
				timeout_ms: 120000,
				want: "",
			})
			faults = find_faults!(row, result)
			if faults.is_empty() {
				Shale.print!("ok   ${pattern}")
			} else {
				Shale.print!("FAIL ${pattern}: ${Str.join_with(faults, "; ")}")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
				Shale.print!(result.out)
			}
		}
		if !(rows.any(|row| row.findings > 0)) {
			Shale.print!("FAIL `unused_import` has no plant")
			$wrong = $wrong + 1
		}
		if $wrong > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("find_unused_imports self_test: ${$wrong.to_str()} wrong")
		}
		row_count = rows.len().to_str()
		proof = "each plant gives its findings and a nonzero exit, each clean case none and exit 0"
		Shale.print!("find_unused_imports self_test: PASS (${row_count} rows: ${proof})")
	}
}

## The launcher, which the self-test runs each plant through.
launcher : Str
launcher = "cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale"

plants : Str
plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_unused_imports/"

## A plant's run: its files below `plants`, the findings it must print, the
## literals its output must hold, and whether it must stop without a finding.
Row : {
	plant : Str,
	findings : U64,
	says : List(Str),
	stops : Bool,
}

## A plant with no finding to give.
quiet : Str -> Row
quiet = |plant| {
	plant,
	findings: 0,
	says: [],
	stops: Bool.False,
}

## A plant with one finding, and what it says.
fires_once : Str, Str -> Row
fires_once = |plant, saying| {
	plant,
	findings: 1,
	says: [saying],
	stops: Bool.False,
}

rows : List(Row)
rows = [
	fires_once("unused.roc", "unused.roc:3: unused_import: `game.Polygon` is imported"),
	fires_once("unused_alias.roc", "`game.Distance` as `D` is imported and never used"),
	fires_once("unused_exposing.roc", "`pf.Stdout` is imported"),
	fires_once("unused_file_import.roc", "the file import `page` is imported"),
	fires_once("unused_in_prose.roc", "`game.Polygon` is imported"),
	fires_once("unused_method_only.roc", "`game.Distance` is imported"),
	fires_once("unused_tag_namesake.roc", "`game.Other` is imported"),
	fires_once("unused_beside_hosted.roc", "unused_beside_hosted.roc:24: unused_import: `Http`"),
	{

## The last line of `out` that isn't one of Shale's `──` lines.
last_said : Str -> Str
last_said = |out|
	out.trim().split_on("\n").fold(
		"",
		|last, line|
			if line.starts_with("──") or line.trim() == "" {
				last
			} else {
				line
			},
	)

## What is wrong with one row's run (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `row_faults`).
find_faults! : Row, { code : I64, out : Str } => List(Str)
find_faults! = |row, result| {
	must_fail = row.stops or row.findings > 0
	var $faults = []
	if must_fail and result.code == 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited 0")
	}
	if !(must_fail) and result.code != 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited ${result.code.to_str()}")
	}
	found = Shale.re_lines!(result.out, "^[^ ]+:[0-9]+: unused_import: ").len()
	if found != row.findings {
		printed = "unused_import printed ${found.to_str()}"
		$faults = $faults.append("${printed}, not ${row.findings.to_str()}")
	}
	if !(row.stops) and !(last_said(result.out).contains(" files; ")) {
		$faults = $faults.append("its last line is no summary: ${last_said(result.out)}")
	}
	for literal in row.says {
		if !(result.out.contains(literal)) {
			$faults = $faults.append("its output lacks `${literal}`")
		}
	}
	$faults
}

-- This recipe finds import lines that the file never uses, since Roc doesn't
-- warn of one.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports.shale
--   shale cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob       the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default; several globs may
--              be given, separated by commas;
--   self_test  with `self_test=1`, check the plants in
--              `cookbook/roc/plants/find_unused_imports/`.
--
-- The check:
--
--   unused_import  An `import` line whose name the file never refers to. The
--              name is the alias of `import pkg.Mod as M`, else the last part
--              of the module's path: `Mod` of `import pkg.Mod` and of
--              `import Mod`. A use is a value, tag or type whose first part
--              is that name: `Mod.name`, `Mod.Type`, `Mod.Tag(x)`, the
--              module's own type `Mod`, in an annotation, a pattern, an
--              expect or an interpolation alike. A name the line exposes
--              (`exposing [line!]`) and the file uses is a use of the line.
--              A file import, `import "page.html" as page : Str`, is used
--              when the file refers to `page`. An entry of a platform
--              header's `hosted { ... }` block uses the module it names
--              (`"sym": Host.f!` uses `Host`). A name in a comment or a
--              string is no use.
--
-- A method call never names its module, so a module whose only use is a
-- method on a value of its type is unused here, and Roc agrees: the method
-- resolves through the value's type without the import. A bare tag that
-- shares a module's name (`Other`, in an expression, a pattern or a tag union
-- type) is no use of the module, but a nominal type's name before its record
-- (`Point.{ x: 0 }`) is.
--
-- roc-ast drops the qualifier of a tag in a pattern (`Color.Red =>` comes as
-- `.Red`), so that name is read from the source at the pattern's column.
--
-- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again
-- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if
-- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way.
-- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./gate_recipe.shale")
use("./imports.shale")
const CHECKS = {"unused_import"}

function judge_file(f, report)
  for imp in unused_imports(f.nodes, split(read(f.path), "\n")) do
    push(report, {path = f.path, line = imp.line, check = "unused_import", what = imp.label .. " is imported and never used: delete the line"})
  end
  return nil
end
function self_test()
  local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_unused_imports/"
  check_plants("find_unused_imports", "cookbook:roc/find_unused_imports.shale", CHECKS, {
    {glob = at .. "unused.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"unused.roc:3: unused_import: `game.Polygon` is imported and never used"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_alias.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Distance` as `D` is imported and never used"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_exposing.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`pf.Stdout` is imported"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_file_import.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"the file import `page` is imported"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_in_prose.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Polygon` is imported"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_method_only.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Distance` is imported"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_tag_namesake.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"`game.Other` is imported"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused_beside_hosted.roc", counts = {unused_import = 1}, says = {"unused_beside_hosted.roc:24: unused_import: `Http` is imported"}},
    {glob = at .. "unused.roc," .. at .. "unused_alias.roc", counts = {unused_import = 2}},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_qualified.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_annotation.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_expect.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_pattern_tag.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_tag.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_exposing.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_alias.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_interpolation.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_file_import.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "quiet_hosted.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}},
  })
  return nil
end

function run_check()
  local paths = {}
  for g in split(GLOB, ",") do
    for p in glob(trim(g)) do push(paths, p) end
  end
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths)
  local report = {}
  for f in parsed.files do judge_file(f, report) end
  local verdict = verdict_of("find_unused_imports", CHECKS, report, #paths)
  print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found)
  fail_if_refused("find_unused_imports", parsed.refused)
  return verdict
end

-- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a
-- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it.
if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
else
  local verdict = run_check()
  if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end
end

## cookbook/roc/check_module_size.shale, ported to Roc on Shale's platform:
## each Roc module held to a size, 500 lines at most, the whole file
## counted. Its header says the rules; this port keeps its arguments, its
## output and its stops, and leaves out `self_test` (the original's plants
## stay its own).
##
##   shale roc_platform/run.shale script=roc_platform/examples/check_module_size.roc glob=app/**/*.roc
##
## The arguments: `glob` (commas between several, `**/*.roc` by default),
## `tests` (`*Spec.roc,test/`), `exempt` (an exemptions file, `path --
## reason` a line), `limit` (500) and `all` (`all=1` lists every module).
## budget: steps=50000000 reads=100000
app [main!] { pf: platform "../platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	limit_text = Shale.arg!("limit", "500")
	limit = match U64.from_str(limit_text) {
		Ok(n) => n
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("check_module_size: limit=${limit_text} is no number")
			0
		}
	}
	opts = {
		glob: Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc"),
		tests: Shale.arg!("tests", "*Spec.roc,test/"),
		exempt: Shale.arg!("exempt", ""),
		limit,
	}
	all = Shale.arg!("all", "") == "1"
	r = module_sizes!(opts)
	if all {
		for l in r.listing {
			Shale.print!(l)
		}
	}
	print_findings!(r.summary, r.found)
	if !(List.is_empty(r.found)) {
		Shale.fail!(r.summary)
	}
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale).
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, found| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(List.is_empty(found)) {
		for l in found {
			Shale.print!(l)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

comma_items : Str -> List(Str)
comma_items = |s|
	Str.split_on(s, ",")
		.map(Str.trim)
		.keep_if(|x| !(Str.is_empty(x)))

## Whether `path` is in one of the test roots: a folder anywhere in it (`x/`),
## a file name's ending (`*X`), or a whole file name.
in_test_root : Str, List(Str) -> Bool
in_test_root = |path, roots| {
	base = basename(path)
	List.any(
		roots,
		|r|
			if Str.ends_with(r, "/") {
				Str.starts_with(path, r) or Str.contains(path, "/${r}") or Str.contains(path, ":${r}")
			} else if Str.starts_with(r, "*") {
				Str.ends_with(base, Str.drop_prefix(r, "*"))
			} else {
				base == r
			},
	)
}

basename : Str -> Str
basename = |path|
	match List.last(Str.split_on(path, "/")) {
		Ok(b) => b
		Err(_) => path
	}

Exemption : { path : Str, reason : Str }

## The exemptions, each `path -- reason`; a malformed line, a missing path or
## one given twice stops the run.
exemptions_of! : Str => List(Exemption)
exemptions_of! = |file| {
	if file == "" {
		return []
	}
	text = match Shale.read!(file) {
		Found(t) => t
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("check_module_size: no exemptions file ${file}")
			""
		}
	}
	var $out = []
	var $number = 0
	for raw in lines(text) {
		$number = $number + 1
		l = Str.trim(raw)
		if l != "" and !(Str.starts_with(l, "#")) {
			place = "${file}:${U64.to_str($number)}: "
			match Str.split_first(l, " -- ") {
				Ok({ before, after }) => {
					reason = Str.trim(after)
					path = Str.trim(before)
					if reason == "" {
						Shale.fail!("check_module_size: ${place}expected `path -- reason`, got `${l}`")
					}
					if !(Shale.exists!(path)) {
						Shale.fail!("check_module_size: ${place}`${path}` is no file")
					}
					if List.any($out, |e| e.path == path) {
						Shale.fail!("check_module_size: ${place}`${path}` is exempted twice")
					}
					$out = $out.append({ path, reason })
				}
				Err(_) => Shale.fail!("check_module_size: ${place}expected `path -- reason`, got `${l}`")
			}
		}
	}
	$out
}

## A text's lines, as Shale's `lines` splits it: a last newline ends a line,
## it does not begin one.
lines : Str -> List(Str)
lines = |text| {
	parts = Str.split_on(text, "\n")
	if Str.ends_with(text, "\n") {
		List.sublist(parts, { start: 0, len: List.len(parts) - 1 })
	} else {
		parts
	}
}

## A file's lines as Shale's `count_lines` counts them: the newlines, and a
## last line that has none.
count_lines : Str -> U64
count_lines = |text| {
	bytes = Str.to_utf8(text)
	newlines = List.count_if(bytes, |b| b == 10)
	match List.last(bytes) {
		Ok(10) => newlines
		Ok(_) => newlines + 1
		Err(_) => 0
	}
}

## Bytewise order, as Shale's `sort` puts strings.
byte_order : Str, Str -> [Before, Same, After]
byte_order = |a, b| {
	x = Str.to_utf8(a)
	y = Str.to_utf8(b)
	var $k = 0
	var $answer = Same
	var $going = Bool.True
	while $going {
		match (List.get(x, $k), List.get(y, $k)) {
			(Ok(p), Ok(q)) =>
				if p < q {
					$answer = Before
					$going = Bool.False
				} else if p > q {
					$answer = After
					$going = Bool.False
				} else {
					$k = $k + 1
				}
			(Err(_), Ok(_)) => {
				$answer = Before
				$going = Bool.False
			}
			(Ok(_), Err(_)) => {
				$answer = After
				$going = Bool.False
			}
			(Err(_), Err(_)) => {
				$going = Bool.False
			}
		}
	}
	$answer
}

## The paths the globs name, each once, sorted, build output left out.
module_paths! : Str => List(Str)
module_paths! = |globs| {
	var $seen = []
	for g in comma_items(globs) {
		for p in Shale.glob!(g) {
			if !(Str.contains(p, "zig-out/")) and !(Str.contains(p, "node_modules/")) and !(List.contains($seen, p)) {
				$seen = $seen.append(p)
			}
		}
	}
	List.sort_with($seen, byte_order)
}

module_sizes! : { glob : Str, tests : Str, exempt : Str, limit : U64 } => { summary : Str, found : List(Str), listing : List(Str) }
module_sizes! = |opts| {
	exemptions = exemptions_of!(opts.exempt)
	roots = comma_items(opts.tests)
	limit = opts.limit
	limit_s = U64.to_str(limit)
	var $found = []
	var $listing = []
	var $modules = 0
	var $tests = 0
	var $over = 0
	var $exempt = 0
	var $unneeded = 0
	for path in module_paths!(opts.glob) {
		n = match Shale.read!(path) {
			Found(text) => count_lines(text)
			Missing => 0
		}
		n_s = U64.to_str(n)
		if in_test_root(path, roots) {
			$tests = $tests + 1
			$listing = $listing.append("${path}: ${n_s} lines, a test root's, no limit")
		} else {
			$modules = $modules + 1
			var $note = ""
			match List.find_first(exemptions, |e| e.path == path) {
				Ok(e) => {
					$exempt = $exempt + 1
					$note = " (exempt: ${e.reason})"
					if n <= limit {
						$unneeded = $unneeded + 1
						$found = $found.append("${path}: unneeded_exemption: ${n_s} lines (limit ${limit_s}) needs no exemption")
					}
				}
				Err(_) =>
					if n > limit {
						$over = $over + 1
						$found = $found.append("${path}: module_size: ${n_s} lines (limit ${limit_s})")
					}
			}
			$listing = $listing.append("${path}: ${n_s} lines${$note}")
		}
	}
	summary = "check_module_size (Roc): ${U64.to_str($modules)} modules, ${U64.to_str($tests)} test files left out; module_size ${U64.to_str($over)} over ${limit_s} lines, ${U64.to_str($exempt)} exempt, unneeded_exemption ${U64.to_str($unneeded)}"
	{ summary, found: $found, listing: $listing }
}
