It also imports Finding, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/find_bare_floats/find_bare_floats.roc, 116 lines

## find_bare_floats, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## every bare `F64` in a project's declarations, for a project that keeps its
## floats inside unit types, where a `Metres` says what an `F64` doesn't.
## What must stay a float is named in the project's table, with a reason. Its
## launcher, cookbook/roc/find_bare_floats.shale, is how it is run, and its
## header says the rules, `bare_float` and `unused_exception`.
## check_goldens.shale, beside this, holds its output on the plants to its
## goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale table=bare_floats.txt
##   shale cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `table` (the project's exceptions)
## and `self_test` (`self_test=1` runs the plants, each through the
## launcher).
##
## This root reads the table (`Shale.read!`), globs the files
## (`Shale.glob!`), has Roc's parser read them (`Shale.roc_tree!`), and
## prints the verdict (`Shale.print!`, `Shale.fail!`). Its modules are
## beside it: the rule (Floats), what it spares (TestHelpers, Exceptions)
## and SelfTest; what they read (Tree, Text) and Finding are the cookbook's
## Roc library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 programs=100
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import Exceptions
import lib.Finding
import Floats
import SelfTest
import lib.Tree

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	if Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1" {
		SelfTest.run!(checks)
	} else {
		run_check!({})
	}
}

## The check over the glob's files: the verdict printed, then a stop when a
## file didn't parse, or when there are findings, the summary the last line
## a caller reads. The table is read before the files are globbed, so a bad
## table stops the run before anything is judged.
run_check! : {} => {}
run_check! = |{}| {
	exceptions = Exceptions.read!(Shale.arg!("table", ""))
	paths = Shale.glob!(Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc"))
	var $findings = []
	var $covered = []
	var $read_modules = Set.empty()
	$in_helpers : U64
	var $in_helpers = 0
	var $refused = []
	for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if file.err == "" {
			$read_modules = $read_modules.insert(Tree.module_name(file.path))
			judged = Floats.judge_file({ path: file.path, syntax_nodes: file.nodes }, exceptions)
			$findings = $findings.concat(judged.findings)
			$covered = $covered.concat(judged.covered)
			$in_helpers = $in_helpers + judged.in_helpers
		} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
			$refused = $refused.append(file.err)
		} else {
			$refused = $refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}")
		}
	}
	unused = Exceptions.find_unused!(
		exceptions,
		{ read_modules: $read_modules, used: Set.from_list($covered) },
	)
	if $in_helpers > 0 {
		spared = "bare `F64`s are in helpers only tests use"
		Shale.print!("${$in_helpers.to_str()} ${spared}, and aren't judged")
	}
	report = $findings.concat(unused)
	found = report.sort_with(Finding.order).map(Finding.line_of)
	summary = summary_of(report, paths.len())
	print_findings!(summary, found)
	if !($refused.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in $refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		refusals = "roc-ast refused ${$refused.len().to_str()} files (named above)"
		why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
		Shale.fail!("find_bare_floats: ${refusals}, ${why}")
	}
	if !(found.is_empty()) {
		Shale.fail!(summary)
	}
}

## The checks, in the order the summary counts them.
checks : List(Str)
checks = ["bare_float", "unused_exception"]

## The counts, `find_bare_floats (Roc): N files; bare_float N,
## unused_exception N`.
summary_of : List(Finding), U64 -> Str
summary_of = |findings, file_count| {
	"find_bare_floats (Roc): ${file_count.to_str()} files; ${Finding.counts_of(findings, checks)}"
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/find_bare_floats/Exceptions.roc, 124 lines

## A project's table of the floats that stay floats (`table=`), read: each
## line `Name: reason`, a name a module or what is in it (`Pixels`,
## `Scene.fade`, `Animation.Spot.lift`). The longest line that fits a
## finding answers for it, and a line no finding needs, or one naming a
## module no file below the table's folder holds, is a finding of its own,
## `unused_exception`.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

Exceptions := { path : Str, excuses : List(Exceptions.Excuse) }.{

	## A table's line, excusing a name's floats: the name, the module that name
	## starts with, and the line's number.
	Excuse : {
		name : Str,
		module_name : Str,
		line : U64,
	}

	## The table at `path`, empty when `path` is `""`. A missing table, a line
	## with no reason and a name listed twice each stop the run.
	read! : Str => Exceptions
	read! = |path| {
		if path == "" {
			return { path, excuses: [] }
		}
		if !(Shale.exists!(path)) {
			Shale.fail!("find_bare_floats: no table ${path}")
		}
		text = match Shale.read!(path) {
			Found(found) => found
			Missing => {
				Shale.fail!("find_bare_floats: no table ${path}")
				""
			}
		}
		var $excuses = []
		$number : U64
		var $number = 0
		for raw in Text.lines(text) {
			$number = $number + 1
			line = Text.trim(raw)
			if line != "" and !(line.starts_with("#")) {
				line_place = "find_bare_floats: ${path}:${$number.to_str()}"
				name = match Shale.re_find!(line, name_pattern) {
					Found(found) => excused_name(found.groups)
					NoMatch => {
						Shale.fail!("${line_place}: expected `Name: reason`")
						""
					}
				}
				if $excuses.any(|excuse| excuse.name == name) {
					Shale.fail!("${line_place}: `${name}` is listed twice")
				}
				module_name = name.split_on(".").first() ?? name
				$excuses = $excuses.append({ name, module_name, line: $number })
			}
		}
		{ path, excuses: $excuses }
	}

	## The longest name of the table that covers `key`, a dotted name: `key`
	## itself, or the part of it before one of its dots.
	cover : Exceptions, Str -> Try(Str, [Uncovered])
	cover = |exceptions, key| {
		parts = key.split_on(".")
		var $count = parts.len()
		while $count >= 1 {
			name = Str.join_with(parts.take_first($count), ".")
			if exceptions.excuses.any(|excuse| excuse.name == name) {
				return Ok(name)
			}
			$count = $count - 1
		}
		Err(Uncovered)
	}

	## The table's lines that excuse nothing: each naming a module no file
	## below the table's folder holds, or, for a module the run read, a name
	## no finding needed (`used`). A line for a module the run didn't read
	## isn't judged.
	find_unused! : Exceptions, { read_modules : Set(Str), used : Set(Str) } => List(Finding)
	find_unused! = |exceptions, run| {
		if exceptions.excuses.is_empty() {
			return []
		}
		below = Text.path_under(Text.dirname(exceptions.path), "**/*.roc")
		known = Set.from_list(Shale.glob!(below).map(Tree.module_name))
		finding_at = |excuse, what| {
			path: exceptions.path,
			line: excuse.line,
			check: "unused_exception",
			what: "`${excuse.name}` ${what}",
		}
		var $found = []
		for excuse in exceptions.excuses {
			is_known = known.contains(excuse.module_name)
			is_needed = run.used.contains(excuse.name)
			is_read = run.read_modules.contains(excuse.module_name)
			if !is_known {
				$found = $found.append(finding_at(excuse, "names a module no file here holds"))
			}
			if is_known and is_read and !is_needed {
				$found = $found.append(finding_at(excuse, "excuses nothing: no finding needs it"))
			}
		}
		$found
	}
}

## A table's line: a name of letters, digits and `_`, its parts joined by
## `.`, a part after the first perhaps ending in `!`, then `:` and a reason.
name_pattern : Str
name_pattern = "^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?)*): +[^ ]"

## The name a match of `name_pattern` holds, its one group.
excused_name : List(Str) -> Str
excused_name = |groups|
	match groups.first() {
		Ok(name) => name
		Err(_) => crash "find_bare_floats: the table's pattern has a group, the name"
	}

cookbook/roc/find_bare_floats/Floats.roc, 145 lines

## The rule, `bare_float`: an `F64` in a top-level or member annotation or in
## a type declaration, however deep in the type (a field, a list's element, a
## tag's payload), each `F64` a finding, unless the table excuses it or a
## helper only tests use holds it. A local's annotation is the body's
## business and isn't judged.
import Exceptions
import lib.Finding
import TestHelpers
import lib.Tree

Floats := [].{

	## A file Roc's parser read: its path and its tree.
	ParsedFile : { path : Str, syntax_nodes : List(Tree.Node) }

	## What a file's floats give: the findings, the table's names that excused
	## one, and how many sit in helpers only tests use.
	Judged : {
		findings : List(Finding),
		covered : List(Str),
		in_helpers : U64,
	}

	## Each `F64` of the file judged.
	judge_file : Floats.ParsedFile, Exceptions -> Floats.Judged
	judge_file = |file, exceptions| {
		var $float_places = []
		$at : U64
		var $at = 0
		for node in file.syntax_nodes {
			$at = $at + 1
			if node.kind == "ty" and Tree.last_part(Tree.attribute(node, "name")) == "F64" {
				$float_places = $float_places.append($at)
			}
		}
		if $float_places.is_empty() {
			return { findings: [], covered: [], in_helpers: 0 }
		}
		reading = { file, file_module: Tree.module_name(file.path) }
		helpers = TestHelpers.helper_names(file.syntax_nodes)
		var $findings = []
		var $covered = []
		$in_helpers : U64
		var $in_helpers = 0
		for place in $float_places {
			match declaration_of(reading, place) {
				Err(Local) => {}
				Ok(found) =>
					if !(found.in_type) and helpers.contains(found.name) {
						$in_helpers = $in_helpers + 1
					} else {
						match Exceptions.cover(exceptions, found.key) {
							Ok(name) => {
								$covered = $covered.append(name)
							}
							Err(Uncovered) => {
								$findings = $findings.append(bare_float(file, found))
							}
						}
					}
			}
		}
		{
			findings: $findings,
			covered: $covered,
			in_helpers: $in_helpers,
		}
	}
}

## A file being judged, with the module its name says it holds.
Reading : { file : Floats.ParsedFile, file_module : Str }

## Where a float is declared: `key`, its dotted name (`Scene.Spot.lift`);
## `declaration`, the place of the annotation or type declaration holding
## it, and `name`, that declaration's own; whether a type's block holds it;
## and the float's own line.
Declared : {
	key : Str,
	declaration : U64,
	name : Str,
	in_type : Bool,
	line : U64,
}

## Where the `F64` at `place` is declared, or `Local` when it belongs to a
## local's annotation or a body. A type's own module isn't repeated in its
## key, so `Unit :: F64` in Unit.roc is `Unit`.
declaration_of : Reading, U64 -> Try(Declared, [Local])
declaration_of = |reading, place| {
	syntax_nodes = reading.file.syntax_nodes
	float_node = Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, place)
	var $names = []
	$declaration : U64
	var $declaration = 0
	var $in_type = Bool.False
	var $above = float_node.parent
	while $above != 0 {
		node = Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, $above)
		kind = node.kind
		if kind.starts_with("e-") or kind.starts_with("p-") or kind == "s-decl" {
			return Err(Local)
		}
		if kind == "anno-record-field" or kind == "s-type-anno" {
			$names = [Tree.attribute(node, "name")].concat($names)
		}
		if kind == "s-type-decl" {
			type_name = Tree.attribute(Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 1)), "name")
			if type_name != reading.file_module {
				$names = [type_name].concat($names)
			}
			$in_type = Bool.True
		}
		if (kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl") and $declaration == 0 {
			$declaration = $above
		}
		$above = node.parent
	}
	Ok({
		key: Str.join_with([reading.file_module].concat($names), "."),
		declaration: $declaration,
		name: Tree.attribute(Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, $declaration), "name"),
		in_type: $in_type,
		line: float_node.line,
	})
}

## A `bare_float` finding: the float's key and the declaration's whole type,
## what a reader will find at the line.
bare_float : Floats.ParsedFile, Declared -> Finding
bare_float = |file, found| {
	declaration = Tree.node_at(file.syntax_nodes, found.declaration)
	type_place = if declaration.kind == "s-type-anno" {
		Tree.kid_at(declaration, 1)
	} else {
		Tree.kid_at(declaration, 2)
	}
	type_text = Tree.written_type(file.syntax_nodes, type_place)
	{
		path: file.path,
		line: found.line,
		check: "bare_float",
		what: "`${found.key}` has a bare `F64`: ${type_text}",
	}
}

cookbook/roc/find_bare_floats/SelfTest.roc, 269 lines

## The recipe's self-test: each plant under
## cookbook/roc/plants/find_bare_floats/ run through the launcher, held to its
## findings, its exit and what it says (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `check_plants`). It copies cookbook/roc/check_families/SelfTest.roc's
## runner, on purpose: a row is run through `Shale.run!`, and
## cookbook/roc/lib/, a package, reaches no effect.
import pf.Shale

SelfTest := [].{

	## Each row run as a child of its own, through `launcher`; a check of
	## `checks` no row fires fails too, since it could be blind.
	run! : List(Str) => {}
	run! = |checks| {
		$wrong : U64
		var $wrong = 0
		var $fired = Set.empty()
		for row in rows {
			command = ["shale", launcher, "glob=${row.plant}"].concat(row.arguments)
			result = Shale.run!({
				argv: command,
				keep: Whole(4000000),
				timeout_ms: 120000,
				want: "",
			})
			faults = find_faults!(row, result, checks)
			for (check, _) in row.counts {
				$fired = $fired.insert(check)
			}
			if faults.is_empty() {
				Shale.print!("ok   ${row.plant}")
			} else {
				Shale.print!("FAIL ${row.plant}: ${Str.join_with(faults, "; ")}")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
				Shale.print!(result.out)
			}
		}
		for check in checks {
			if !($fired.contains(check)) {
				Shale.print!("FAIL `${check}` has no plant")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
			}
		}
		if $wrong > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("find_bare_floats self_test: ${$wrong.to_str()} wrong")
		}
		row_count = rows.len().to_str()
		proof = "each plant gives its findings and a nonzero exit, each clean case none and exit 0"
		Shale.print!("find_bare_floats self_test: PASS (${row_count} rows: ${proof})")
	}
}

## The launcher, which the self-test runs each plant through.
launcher : Str
launcher = "cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale"

plants : Str
plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_bare_floats/"

## A plant's run: its files (a glob below `plants`) and its other arguments,
## the findings each check must print, the literals its output must hold,
## and whether it must stop without a finding.
Row : {
	plant : Str,
	arguments : List(Str),
	counts : List((Str, U64)),
	says : List(Str),
	stops : Bool,
}

## A plant's run, before its place below `plants` is spelled out.
Wanted : {
	plant : Str,
	arguments : List(Str),
	counts : List((Str, U64)),
	says : List(Str),
}

## A plant that must give its findings, or none when `counts` is empty.
gives : Wanted -> Row
gives = |wanted| {
	plant: "${plants}${wanted.plant}",
	arguments: wanted.arguments,
	counts: wanted.counts,
	says: wanted.says,
	stops: Bool.False,
}

## What a plant that stops is run with and must say.
Stopping : {
	plant : Str,
	arguments : List(Str),
	says : List(Str),
}

## A plant that must stop before any finding, saying what it says.
stops : Stopping -> Row
stops = |wanted| {
	plant: "${plants}${wanted.plant}",
	arguments: wanted.arguments,
	counts: [],
	says: wanted.says,
	stops: Bool.True,
}

## The table argument for a table below `plants`.
table : Str -> Str
table = |name| "table=${plants}${name}"

rows : List(Row)
rows = [
	gives({
		plant: "Signatures.roc",
		arguments: [],
		counts: [("bare_float", 12)],
		says: [
			"Signatures.roc:5: bare_float: `Signatures.Reading` has a bare `F64`: F64",
			"`Signatures.scaled` has a bare `F64`: (Reading, F64 -> Reading)",

		says: ["`Unit.plus` excuses nothing", "`Vanished` names a module"],
	}),
	stops({ plant: "broken/*.roc", arguments: [], says: ["refused: "] }),
	stops({
		plant: "Quiet.roc",
		arguments: [table("no_such.txt")],
		says: ["no table"],
	}),
	stops({
		plant: "Quiet.roc",
		arguments: [table("table_no_reason.txt")],
		says: ["table_no_reason.txt:2: expected"],
	}),
	stops({
		plant: "Quiet.roc",
		arguments: [table("table_twice.txt")],
		says: ["`Quiet.name` is listed twice"],
	}),
]

## The last line of `out` that isn't one of Shale's `──` lines.
last_said : Str -> Str
last_said = |out|
	out.trim().split_on("\n").fold(
		"",
		|last, line|
			if line.starts_with("──") or line.trim() == "" {
				last
			} else {
				line
			},
	)

## The findings `row` wants of `check`.
wanted_count : Row, Str -> U64
wanted_count = |row, check| {
	$wanted : U64
	var $wanted = 0
	for (counted, count) in row.counts {
		if counted == check {
			$wanted = count
		}
	}
	$wanted
}

## What is wrong with one row's run (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `row_faults`).
find_faults! : Row, { code : I64, out : Str }, List(Str) => List(Str)
find_faults! = |row, result, checks| {
	must_fail = row.stops or !(row.counts.is_empty())
	var $faults = []
	if must_fail and result.code == 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited 0")
	}
	if !(must_fail) and result.code != 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited ${result.code.to_str()}")
	}
	for check in checks {
		found = Shale.re_lines!(result.out, "^[^ ]+:[0-9]+: ${check}: ").len()
		wanted = wanted_count(row, check)
		if found != wanted {
			$faults = $faults.append("${check} printed ${found.to_str()}, not ${wanted.to_str()}")
		}
	}
	if !(row.stops) and !(last_said(result.out).contains(" files; ")) {
		$faults = $faults.append("its last line is no summary: ${last_said(result.out)}")
	}
	for literal in row.says {
		if !(result.out.contains(literal)) {
			$faults = $faults.append("its output lacks `${literal}`")
		}
	}
	$faults
}

## The helpers only tests use, whose floats aren't judged. A helper is a
## definition at the top level of a type module, outside the type's block,
## which the compiler lets no other module reach, so the file's own tree
## shows everything that uses it. It is one when every use is in an `expect`
## or in another such helper, and there is one. An app's or a `module [...]`
## file's top-level names can be reached from outside, so they have none. A
## local that shares a helper's name counts as a use, which can only report
## more.
import lib.Tree

TestHelpers := [].{

	## The names of the file's helpers only tests use.
	helper_names : List(Tree.Node) -> Set(Str)
	helper_names = |nodes| {
		if !(is_type_module(nodes)) {
			return Set.empty()
		}
		definitions = top_level_definitions(nodes)
		uses = places_of_uses(nodes, definitions)
		var $helpers = Set.from_list(
			uses
				.to_list()
				.keep_if(|(_, places)| !(places.is_empty()))
				.map(|(name, _)| name),
		)
		# A helper falls when anything outside tests uses it, which can bring
		# down the helpers only it used.
		var $changed = Bool.True
		while $changed {
			$changed = Bool.False
			for (name, places) in uses.to_list() {
				if $helpers.contains(name) {
					var $falls = Bool.False
					for place in places.to_list() {
						if place != in_a_test and !($helpers.contains(place)) {
							$falls = Bool.True
						}
					}
					if $falls {
						$helpers = $helpers.remove(name)
						$changed = Bool.True
					}
				}
			}
		}
		$helpers
	}
}

## The place of a node inside a test.
in_a_test : Str
in_a_test = "expect"

## The place of a node in neither a definition nor a test.
in_no_definition : Str
in_no_definition = ""

## The place of a node's parent, which comes before it.
place_of_parent : List(Str), Tree.Node -> Str
place_of_parent = |places, node|
	match places.get(node.parent - 1) {
		Ok(place) => place
		Err(_) => crash "find_bare_floats: a node before its parent"
	}

## Whether the file is a type module, with a `type-mod` header.
is_type_module : List(Tree.Node) -> Bool
is_type_module = |nodes|
	Tree.node_at(nodes, 1).kids.any(|kid| Tree.node_at(nodes, kid).kind == "type-mod")

## The definitions at the top level of the file, outside any type's block:
## each name with its `s-decl`'s place, the last one where a name is defined
## twice.
top_level_definitions : List(Tree.Node) -> Dict(Str, U64)
top_level_definitions = |nodes| {
	var $found = Dict.empty()
	for top in Tree.node_at(nodes, 1).kids {
		statements = Tree.node_at(nodes, top)
		if statements.kind == "statements" {
			for place in statements.kids {
				statement = Tree.node_at(nodes, place)
				if statement.kind == "s-decl" {
					match statement.kids.first() {
						Ok(pattern_place) => {
							pattern = Tree.node_at(nodes, pattern_place)
							if pattern.kind == "p-ident" {
								$found = $found.insert(Tree.attribute(pattern, "raw"), place)
							}
						}
						Err(_) => {}
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	$found
}

## Where each definition is used: its name with the places of its uses, a
## place being the definition the use sits in, `in_a_test` in a test, and
## `""` anywhere else. A definition's use of itself is no place. A parent
## comes before its kids, so one pass gives each node its place.
places_of_uses : List(Tree.Node), Dict(Str, U64) -> Dict(Str, Set(Str))
places_of_uses = |nodes, definitions| {
	var $defined_at = Dict.empty()
	for (name, place) in definitions.to_list() {
		$defined_at = $defined_at.insert(place, name)
	}
	var $uses = Dict.empty()
	for (name, _) in definitions.to_list() {
		$uses = $uses.insert(name, Set.empty())
	}
	var $places = []
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	for node in nodes {
		$at = $at + 1
		above = if node.parent == 0 {
			""
		} else {
			place_of_parent($places, node)
		}
		in_test = if node.kind == "s-expect" {
			in_a_test
		} else {
			above
		}
		here = if in_test == "" {
			match $defined_at.get($at) {
				Ok(name) => name
				Err(_) => in_no_definition
			}
		} else {
			in_test
		}
		$places = $places.append(here)
		used = name_used(node)
		if used != "" and used != here {
			match $uses.get(used) {
				Ok(places) => {
					$uses = $uses.insert(used, places.insert(here))
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		}
	}
	$uses
}

## The name a node uses, or `""`: an identifier, or a field in a record's
## short form, `{ a, b }`, which uses `a` and `b`.
name_used : Tree.Node -> Str
name_used = |node|
	if node.kind == "e-ident" {
		Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	} else if node.kind == "field" and node.kids.is_empty() {
		Tree.attribute(node, "field")
	} else {
		""
	}

-- This recipe finds every bare `F64` in a project's declarations, for a project
-- that keeps its floats inside unit types. What must stay a float is named in
-- the project's table, with a reason.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale table=bare_floats.txt
--   shale cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob       the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default;
--   table      the project's exceptions, without which every `F64` is a finding;
--   self_test  with `self_test=1`, check the plants in
--              `cookbook/roc/plants/find_bare_floats/`.
--
-- Each line of the table is `Name: reason`. A name is a module, or what is in
-- it: `Pixels`, `Scene.fade`, `Animation.Spot.lift`. A type's own module isn't
-- repeated, so `to_metres` in `Distance.roc` is `Distance.to_metres`, whether
-- or not it is a member of the type `Distance`. A record field's name follows
-- what declares it. A line covers its name and whatever is inside it, and only
-- the longest line that fits a finding answers for it. A blank line or one
-- starting with `#` is skipped, and a line with no reason or a name listed
-- twice stops the run.
--
-- The checks:
--
--   bare_float        An `F64` in a top-level or member annotation or in a type
--                     declaration, however deep in the type: a field, a list's
--                     element, a tag's payload. Each `F64` is a finding, so a
--                     signature with two gives two. A local's annotation is the
--                     body's business and isn't judged. A constant with no
--                     annotation has no signature, so it can't be judged.
--   unused_exception  A line of the table that no finding needs, or that names
--                     a module no file below the table's folder holds. A line
--                     for a module the run didn't read isn't judged, so a run
--                     over part of a tree still fails only for what it read.
--
-- A helper only tests use is test code and isn't judged, and a line tells it
-- so at the top of the output. It is a definition at the top level of a type
-- module, outside the type's block, which the compiler lets no other module
-- reach, so a file's own text shows everything that uses it. Every use must be
-- in an `expect` or in another such helper, and there must be one. The file has
-- to be a type module for this: an app's or a `module [...]` file's top-level
-- names can be reached from outside, so its helpers are always judged. A local
-- that shares a helper's name counts as a use, which can only report more.
--
-- The output is the counts, one line per finding, and the counts again
-- (cookbook/findings.shale). The run fails if there are findings, or if
-- any file doesn't parse, and the files that do parse are judged either way.
-- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const TABLE_FILE = arg("table", "")
use("./declared.shale")
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./gate_recipe.shale")
const CHECKS = {"bare_float", "unused_exception"}

-- The table as `{lines, by_name, used}`: its lines in order, each `{name,
-- module, line}`, the same by name, and an empty set `judge_float` fills.
function exception_table(path)
  local lines_of_table = {}
  local by_name = {}
  if path == "" then return {lines = lines_of_table, by_name = by_name, used = {}} end
  if not exists(path) then fail("find_bare_floats: no table " .. path) end
  local number = 0
  for raw in lines(read(path)) do
    number = number + 1
    local l = trim(raw)
    if l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then
      local m = re_find(l, "^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?)*): +[^ ]")
      if m == nil then fail("find_bare_floats: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": expected `Name: reason`") end
      if has_key(by_name, m.group) then fail("find_bare_floats: " .. path .. ":" .. number .. ": `" .. m.group .. "` is listed twice") end
      local entry = {name = m.group, module = split(m.group, ".")[1], line = number}
      push(lines_of_table, entry)
      by_name[m.group] = entry
    end
  end
  return {lines = lines_of_table, by_name = by_name, used = {}}
end

-- The longest name of the table that covers `key`, or nil.
function exception_for(exceptions, key)
  local parts = split(key, ".")
  local n = #parts
  while n >= 1 do
    local name = join(take(parts, n), ".")
    if has_key(exceptions.by_name, name) then return name end
    n = n - 1
  end
  return nil
end

function is_type_module(tree)
  for at in children(tree, 1) do
    if tree[at].kind == "type-mod" then return true end
  end
  return false
end

-- Where the `F64` at `at` is declared, or nil when it belongs to a local. `key`
-- is its dotted name, `declaration` the annotation or type declaration holding
-- it, `name` that declaration's own name, and `in_type` whether a type's block
-- holds it.
function declaration_of(tree, at, module)
  local names = {}
  local declaration = 0
  local in_type = false
  local k = tree[at].parent
  while k ~= 0 do
    local kind = tree[k].kind
    if starts_with(kind, "e-") or starts_with(kind, "p-") or kind == "s-decl" then return nil end
    if kind == "anno-record-field" or kind == "s-type-anno" then push(names, attribute(tree, k, "name")) end
    if kind == "s-type-decl" then
      local type_name = attribute(tree, children(tree, k)[1], "name")
      if type_name ~= module then push(names, type_name) end
      in_type = true
    end
    if (kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl") and declaration == 0 then declaration = k end
    k = tree[k].parent
  end
  local parts = {module}
  local i = #names
  while i >= 1 do
    push(parts, names[i])
    i = i - 1
  end
  return {key = join(parts, "."), declaration = declaration, in_type = in_type, name = attribute(tree, declaration, "name")}
end

-- The node's type as text, for a finding: what a reader will find at the line.
function declared_type_text(tree, at)
  local kids = children(tree, at)
  if tree[at].kind == "s-type-anno" then return render_type(tree, kids[1]) end
  return render_type(tree, kids[2])
end

-- The name a node uses, or "": an identifier, or a field in a record's short
-- form, `{ a, b }`, which uses `a` and `b`.
function name_used(tree, at)
  local node = tree[at]
  if node.kind == "e-ident" then return node.raw end
  if node.kind == "field" and #node.kids == 0 then return get(node, "field", "") end
  return ""
end

-- The definitions at the top level of the file, outside any type's block, as a
-- map from each name to its `s-decl`.
function top_level_definitions(tree)
  local found = {}
  for at in children(tree, 1) do
    if tree[at].kind == "statements" then
      for s in children(tree, at) do
        if tree[s].kind == "s-decl" then
          local kids = children(tree, s)
          if #kids > 0 and tree[kids[1]].kind == "p-ident" then found[attribute(tree, kids[1], "raw")] = s end
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return found
end

-- The helpers only tests use, by the rule the header gives: a map from each
-- top-level definition to whether it is one.
-- Each node's `place` is the helper it sits in, `expect` in a test, and "" for
-- anything else. A parent comes before its children, so one pass fills it.
function test_only_helpers(tree)
  local helpers = {}
  if not is_type_module(tree) then return helpers end
  local definitions = top_level_definitions(tree)
  local definition_at = {}
  for name in keys(definitions) do definition_at[tostring(definitions[name])] = name end
  local place = {}
  local places_of = {}
  for name in keys(definitions) do places_of[name] = {} end
  for i = 1, #tree do
    local node = tree[i]
    local here = node.parent == 0 and "" or place[node.parent]
    if node.kind == "s-expect" then here = "expect" end
    if here == "" and has_key(definition_at, tostring(i)) then here = definition_at[tostring(i)] end
    push(place, here)
    local used = name_used(tree, i)
    if used ~= "" and has_key(places_of, used) and here ~= used then places_of[used][here] = true end
  end
  for name in keys(definitions) do
    helpers[name] = #keys(places_of[name]) > 0
  end
  -- A helper falls when anything outside tests uses it, which can bring down
  -- the helpers only it used.
  local changed = true
  while changed do
    changed = false
    for name in keys(helpers) do
      for used_at in keys(places_of[name]) do
        if helpers[name] and used_at ~= "expect" and not get(helpers, used_at, false) then
          helpers[name] = false
          changed = true
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return helpers
end

-- Judges the one `F64` at `at`, and gives 1 when a test's helper holds it.
function judge_float(f, at, module, helpers, exceptions, report)
  local tree = f.nodes
  local where = declaration_of(tree, at, module)
  if where == nil then return 0 end
  if not where.in_type and get(helpers, where.name, false) then return 1 end
  local covered_by = exception_for(exceptions, where.key)
  if covered_by ~= nil then
    exceptions.used[covered_by] = true
    return 0
  end
  push(report, {path = f.path, line = tree[at].line, check = "bare_float", what = "`" .. where.key .. "` has a bare `F64`: " .. declared_type_text(tree, where.declaration)})
  return 0
end

-- Judges one file, and gives how many of its floats belong to tests' helpers.
function judge_file(f, exceptions, report)
  local tree = f.nodes
  local module = module_name(f.path)
  local helpers = test_only_helpers(tree)
  local in_helpers = 0
  for i = 1, #tree do
    if tree[i].kind == "ty" and last_part(attribute(tree, i, "name")) == "F64" then
      in_helpers = in_helpers + judge_float(f, i, module, helpers, exceptions, report)
    end
  end
  return in_helpers
end

function judge_exceptions(exceptions, read_modules, report)
  if #exceptions.lines == 0 then return nil end
  local known = {}
  for p in glob(path_under(dirname(TABLE_FILE), "**/*.roc")) do known[module_name(p)] = true end
  for e in exceptions.lines do
    if not has_key(known, e.module) then
      push(report, {path = TABLE_FILE, line = e.line, check = "unused_exception", what = "`" .. e.name .. "` names a module no file here holds"})
    elseif has_key(read_modules, e.module) and not has_key(exceptions.used, e.name) then
      push(report, {path = TABLE_FILE, line = e.line, check = "unused_exception", what = "`" .. e.name .. "` excuses nothing: no finding needs it"})
    end
  end
  return nil
end

function self_test()
  local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_bare_floats/"
  local recipe = "cookbook:roc/find_bare_floats.shale"
  local table_arg = "table=" .. at .. "whole/table.txt"
  check_plants("find_bare_floats", recipe, CHECKS, {
    {glob = at .. "Signatures.roc", counts = {bare_float = 12}, says = {"Signatures.roc:5: bare_float: `Signatures.Reading` has a bare `F64`: F64", "`Signatures.scaled` has a bare `F64`: (Reading, F64 -> Reading)", "`Signatures.Trip.length` has a bare `F64`: { length : F64, name : Str }", "`Signatures.pair` has a bare `F64`: (F64, F64)"}},
    {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "Helpers.roc", counts = {bare_float = 7}, says = {"`Helpers.used_by_a_member` has", "`Helpers.used_by_a_definition` has", "`Helpers.reached_from_production` has", "`Helpers.in_a_short_record` has", "`Helpers.used_by_nothing` has", "`Helpers.only_itself` has", "`Helpers.member_tests_use` has"}},
    {glob = at .. "QuietHelpers.roc", says = {"3 bare `F64`s are in helpers only tests use"}},
    {glob = at .. "helpers_app.roc", counts = {bare_float = 1}, says = {"`helpers_app.only_tests` has"}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", counts = {bare_float = 7}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {table_arg}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/narrow.txt"}, counts = {bare_float = 2}, says = {"`Held.Spot.left_out` has a bare", "`Held.other` has a bare"}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/shadowed.txt"}, counts = {unused_exception = 1}, says = {"`Held` excuses nothing"}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/*.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/unused.txt"}, counts = {unused_exception = 4}, says = {"unused.txt:4: unused_exception: `Held.gone` excuses nothing", "`Unit.plus` excuses nothing", "`Held.Spot.gone` excuses nothing", "`Vanished` names a module no file here holds"}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/Held.roc", args = {table_arg}},
    {glob = at .. "whole/Unit.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "whole/unused.txt"}, counts = {unused_exception = 2}, says = {"`Unit.plus` excuses nothing", "`Vanished` names a module"}},
    {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}},
    {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no table"}},
    {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_no_reason.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"table_no_reason.txt:2: expected"}},
    {glob = at .. "Quiet.roc", args = {"table=" .. at .. "table_twice.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"`Quiet.name` is listed twice"}},
  })
  return nil
end

function run_check()
  local exceptions = exception_table(TABLE_FILE)
  local paths = glob(GLOB)
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths)
  local report = {}
  local read_modules = {}
  local in_helpers = 0
  for f in parsed.files do
    read_modules[module_name(f.path)] = true
    in_helpers = in_helpers + judge_file(f, exceptions, report)
  end
  judge_exceptions(exceptions, read_modules, report)
  if in_helpers > 0 then print(in_helpers .. " bare `F64`s are in helpers only tests use, and aren't judged") end
  local verdict = verdict_of("find_bare_floats", CHECKS, report, #paths)
  print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found)
  fail_if_refused("find_bare_floats", parsed.refused)
  return verdict
end

-- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a
-- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it.
if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
else
  local verdict = run_check()
  if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end
end

## find_extra_parens, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## the parentheses and braceless `if`s that a code emitter leaves in Roc,
## which neither `roc check` nor `roc fmt` sees, found and, with `write=1`,
## rewritten. Its launcher, cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens.shale, is how it
## is run, and its header says the checks (`paren_if`, `wrapped_body`,
## `else_block`, `lambda_if`) and the rewrite. check_goldens.shale, beside
## this, holds its output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_extra_parens.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_extra_parens.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc write=1
##   shale cookbook:roc/find_extra_parens.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `house` (`house=0` leaves out the
## house style, `paren_if` and `lambda_if`), `write` (`write=1` rewrites the
## files) and `self_test` (`self_test=1` checks the plants and rewrites
## copies of them).
##
## This root globs the files (`Shale.glob!`), rewrites them when asked
## (Rewriting, by Edits), reports (Report, by Checks) and prints the verdict
## (`Shale.print!`, `Shale.fail!`); SelfTest is the self-test. Finding, Text
## and Tree are the cookbook's Roc library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=900000000 read_bytes=1000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 programs=100
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import Report
import Rewriting
import SelfTest

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	pattern = if self_test {
		"${SelfTest.plants}/*.roc"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc")
	}
	write = Shale.arg!("write", "") == "1"
	paths = Shale.glob!(pattern)
	settled = if write {
		refuse_house_rewrite!({})
		rewritten = Rewriting.rewrite!(paths, Rewriting.roc_bin!(Bool.False))
		Shale.print!("find_extra_parens: ${rewritten.made.to_str()} edits")
		rewritten.settled
	} else {
		Dict.empty()
	}
	found = Report.make!(paths, settled)
	print_findings!(found.summary, found.findings.map(Finding.line_of))
	fail_if_refused!(found.refused)
	if self_test {
		SelfTest.run!(paths, found)
	}
}

## A rewrite applies our house style, so `house=0` refuses one.
refuse_house_rewrite! : {} => {}
refuse_house_rewrite! = |{}|
	match Report.read_house!({}) {
		Kept => {}
		LeftOut => Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: write=1 applies our house style, so it refuses house=0")
	}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

## The files Roc's parser refused, named, then a stop (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's
## `fail_if_refused`); nothing when it refused none.
fail_if_refused! : List(Str) => {}
fail_if_refused! = |refused|
	if !(refused.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		refusals = "roc-ast refused ${refused.len().to_str()} files (named above)"
		why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
		Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: ${refusals}, ${why}")
	}

cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens/Report.roc, 124 lines

## The findings across a run's files, as the lines the recipe prints, with
## its summary and the files Roc's parser refused. Findings stay in the files'
## order and the tree's, as the Shale original printed them, never sorted.
import pf.Shale
import Checks
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text

Report := [].{

	## A run's report: its summary, its findings (each `path:line: check:
	## source line`) and why each refused file was refused.
	Report : {
		summary : Str,
		findings : List(Finding),
		refused : List(Str),
	}

	## The report over `paths`. Under `house=0`, the house style
	## (cookbook/roc/house.shale's `paren_if` and `lambda_if`) is left out.
	## `settled` is what a rewrite already knows of a file it read last,
	## unchanged since: `""` for no finding, else why it was refused
	## (`Report.refusal_of`); those files are not read again, as Roc's arena
	## frees nothing and a large tree's second parse would not fit beside its
	## first.
	make! : List(Str), Dict(Str, Str) => Report.Report
	make! = |paths, settled| {
		house = Report.read_house!({})
		unsettled = paths.keep_if(|path| !(settled.contains(path)))
		parsed = if unsettled.is_empty() {
			[]
		} else {
			Shale.roc_tree!(unsettled)
		}
		var $findings = []
		var $refused = []
		$next : U64
		var $next = 0
		for path in paths {
			match settled.get(path) {
				Ok(refusal) =>
					if refusal != "" {
						$refused = $refused.append(refusal)
					}
				Err(_) => {
					file = match parsed.get($next) {
						Ok(found) => found
						Err(_) => crash "Report.make!: roc_tree! gave fewer files than it was asked for"
					}
					$next = $next + 1
					if file.err == "" {
						source_lines = Report.read_text!(file.path).split_on("\n")
						for found in Checks.findings_in(file.nodes, source_lines) {
							if is_kept(house, found.check) {
								$findings = $findings.append({
									path: file.path,
									line: found.line,
									check: found.check,
									what: Text.trim(Text.line_at(source_lines, found.line)),
								})
							}
						}
					} else {
						$refused = $refused.append(Report.refusal_of(file.path, file.err))
					}
				}
			}
		}
		house_note = match house {
			Kept => ""
			LeftOut => "; left out as house style: ${Str.join_with(house_style, ", ")}"
		}
		counts = Finding.counts_of($findings, Checks.names)
		summary = "find_extra_parens (Roc): ${paths.len().to_str()} files; ${counts}${house_note}"
		{ summary, findings: $findings, refused: $refused }
	}

	## Why roc-ast refused a file, beginning with its path
	## (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's `parse_roc_files`).
	refusal_of : Str, Str -> Str
	refusal_of = |path, err|
		if err.starts_with(path) {
			err
		} else {
			"${path}: ${err}"
		}

	## Whether `house=0` leaves the house style out (cookbook/roc/house.shale).
	read_house! : {} => [Kept, LeftOut]
	read_house! = |{}| {
		house = Shale.arg!("house", "1")
		if house != "0" and house != "1" {
			Shale.fail!("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not ${house}")
		}
		if house == "0" {
			LeftOut
		} else {
			Kept
		}
	}

	## A file's text; a file gone since the glob stops the run.
	read_text! : Str => Str
	read_text! = |path|
		match Shale.read!(path) {
			Found(text) => text
			Missing => {
				Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: no file ${path}")
				""
			}
		}
}

## The checks that are only our house style (cookbook/roc/house.shale).
house_style : List(Str)
house_style = ["paren_if", "lambda_if"]

## Whether a finding of `check` is reported.
is_kept : [Kept, LeftOut], Str -> Bool
is_kept = |house, check|
	match house {
		Kept => Bool.True
		LeftOut => !(house_style.contains(check))
	}

cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens/Rewriting.roc, 167 lines

## `write=1`: the files rewritten, one check a pass (Edits), each pass's
## files put through `roc fmt`, until a pass changes nothing, because taking
## off one pair of brackets can show the next. The Roc is the tree's own
## (cookbook/roc/pinned.shale), run by its OS path.
import pf.Shale
import Checks
import Edits
import Report
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

Rewriting := [].{

	## Rewrites `paths` until a pass changes nothing, and answers how many
	## edits it made and what it knows of each file it read last: `settled`,
	## `""` for a file with no finding, else why roc-ast refused it
	## (Report.make!'s `settled`). Such a file is read no more, since no edit
	## will touch it, so a large tree is parsed whole once, not four times a
	## pass, which Roc's arena (it frees nothing) would not hold.
	rewrite! : List(Str), Str => { made : U64, settled : Dict(Str, Str) }
	rewrite! = |paths, roc| {
		$made : U64
		var $made = 0
		var $live = paths
		var $settled = Dict.empty()
		var $changed = Bool.True
		while $changed {
			$changed = Bool.False
			for check in Checks.names {
				pass = rewrite_check!($live, check, roc)
				$live = pass.live
				for (path, verdict) in pass.settled {
					$settled = $settled.insert(path, verdict)
				}
				if pass.made > 0 {
					$made = $made + pass.made
					$changed = Bool.True
				}
			}
		}
		{ made: $made, settled: $settled }
	}

	## The OS path of the Roc to rewrite with: in a self-test the pin every
	## recipe's self-test runs (pinned.shale's `SELF_TEST_PIN`, read there),
	## else the one the `roc-version` where the run starts names.
	roc_bin! : Bool => Str
	roc_bin! = |self_test| {
		pin = if self_test {
			self_test_pin!({})
		} else {
			if !(Shale.exists!("roc-version")) {
				Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: no roc-version where the run starts: run it from the repository's root, whose roc-version pins its Roc")
			}
			Text.trim(Report.read_text!("roc-version"))
		}
		roc = "tools:roc-${pin}/roc"
		if !(Shale.exists!(roc)) {
			Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: no ${roc}: install Roc ${pin} into ~/tools/roc-${pin}/ (roc-apps's toolchain release carries it)")
		}
		Shale.real!(roc)
	}
}

## Makes one kind of edit across `paths`, and answers how many it made, which
## files had a finding of any check (the files still worth reading) and what
## is settled of the rest, each `(path, verdict)` as `rewrite!` keeps it.
rewrite_check! : List(Str), Str, Str => { made : U64, live : List(Str), settled : List((Str, Str)) }
rewrite_check! = |paths, check, roc| {
	$made : U64
	var $made = 0
	var $touched = []
	var $live = []
	var $settled = []
	if !(paths.is_empty()) {
		for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
			if file.err == "" {
				done = rewrite_file!({ path: file.path, nodes: file.nodes }, check)
				if done.found_any {
					$live = $live.append(file.path)
				} else {
					$settled = $settled.append((file.path, ""))
				}
				if done.made > 0 {
					$made = $made + done.made
					$touched = $touched.append(file.path)
				}
			} else {
				$settled = $settled.append((file.path, Report.refusal_of(file.path, file.err)))
			}
		}
	}
	if !($touched.is_empty()) {
		format!($touched, roc)
	}
	{ made: $made, live: $live, settled: $settled }
}

## One kind of edit in one file: how many it made, and whether the file had a
## finding of any check. A finding inside another's span of the same kind is
## safe: its brackets are its own.
rewrite_file! : { path : Str, nodes : List(Tree.Node) }, Str => { made : U64, found_any : Bool }
rewrite_file! = |file, check| {
	text = Report.read_text!(file.path)
	source_lines = text.split_on("\n")
	findings = Checks.findings_in(file.nodes, source_lines)
	bytes = text.to_utf8()
	source = { path: file.path, text: bytes, nodes: file.nodes }
	found_any = !(findings.is_empty())
	match Edits.for_check(source, findings, check) {
		Err(why) => {
			Shale.fail!(why)
			{ made: 0, found_any }
		}
		Ok([]) => { made: 0, found_any }
		Ok(edits) =>
			match Edits.applied(bytes, edits) {
				Err(why) => {
					Shale.fail!(why)
					{ made: 0, found_any }
				}
				Ok(rewritten) => {
					Shale.write!(file.path, Str.from_utf8_lossy(rewritten))
					{ made: edits.len(), found_any }
				}
			}
	}
}

## The files put through the tree's own formatter.
format! : List(Str), Str => {}
format! = |paths, roc| {
	var $argv = [roc, "fmt"]
	for path in paths {
		$argv = $argv.append(Shale.real!(path))
	}
	result = Shale.run!({
		argv: $argv,
		keep: Tail(20),
		timeout_ms: 120000,
		want: "roc-pin: the tree's own formatter",
	})
	if result.code != 0 {
		Shale.print!(result.out)
		Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: `${roc} fmt` exited ${result.code.to_str()}")
	}
}

## pinned.shale's `SELF_TEST_PIN`, the one home of the self-tests' Roc.
self_test_pin! : {} => Str
self_test_pin! = |{}| {
	pinned = "cookbook:roc/pinned.shale"
	match Shale.re_find!(Report.read_text!(pinned), "\nconst SELF_TEST_PIN = \"([^\"]+)\"") {
		Found(found) =>
			match found.groups {
				[pin] => pin
				_ => {
					Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: no SELF_TEST_PIN in ${pinned}")
					""
				}
			}
		NoMatch => {
			Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens: no SELF_TEST_PIN in ${pinned}")
			""
		}
	}
}

cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens/SelfTest.roc, 111 lines

## The recipe's self-test, the Shale original's: each plant in
## cookbook/roc/plants/find_extra_parens/ held to its marks (a line ending
## `# paren_if`, `# wrapped_body`, `# else_block` or `# lambda_if` must give
## that finding, and no unmarked line may give one), then the plants copied
## to `scratch:parens/` and rewritten there: every file must still parse, no
## finding may be left, a second rewrite must change nothing, and a plant with
## a `.want` file must come out as it.
import pf.Shale
import Checks
import Report
import Rewriting
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text

SelfTest := [].{

	## The plants, whose `*.roc` a self-test checks.
	plants : Str
	plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_extra_parens"

	## The self-test of `paths`, the plants, given their report.
	run! : List(Str), Report.Report => {}
	run! = |paths, found| {
		marked = check_marks!(paths, found.findings)
		var $wrong = marked.wrong
		if marked.marks == 0 {
			$wrong = $wrong.append("no plant holds a mark")
		}
		if Shale.exists!(scratch) {
			Shale.remove_tree!(scratch)
		}
		Shale.mkdir!(scratch)
		copies = paths.map(copy_of)
		for path in paths {
			Shale.write!(copy_of(path), Report.read_text!(path))
		}
		roc = Rewriting.roc_bin!(Bool.True)
		rewritten = Rewriting.rewrite!(copies, roc)
		left = Report.make!(copies, rewritten.settled)
		for finding in left.findings {
			$wrong = $wrong.append("left after the rewrite: ${Finding.line_of(finding)}")
		}
		for refusal in left.refused {
			$wrong = $wrong.append("the rewrite broke a file: ${refusal}")
		}
		for path in paths {
			want = "${Text.bytes_of(path, { start: 0, count: path.count_utf8_bytes() - 4 })}.want"
			copy = copy_of(path)
			if Shale.exists!(want) and Report.read_text!(copy) != Report.read_text!(want) {
				$wrong = $wrong.append("${copy}: not as ${want}")
			}
		}
		if Rewriting.rewrite!(copies, roc).made != 0 {
			$wrong = $wrong.append("a second rewrite changed something")
		}
		Shale.remove_tree!(scratch)
		for wrong in $wrong {
			Shale.print!("FAIL ${wrong}")
		}
		if !($wrong.is_empty()) {
			Shale.fail!("find_extra_parens self_test: ${$wrong.len().to_str()} plants wrong")
		}
		proof = "each marked line gives its finding, no other line one; the rewrite leaves none, and a second changes nothing"
		Shale.print!("find_extra_parens (Roc) self_test: PASS (${proof})")
	}
}

## Where the self-test rewrites its copies of the plants.
scratch : Str
scratch = "scratch:parens"

## A plant's copy in `scratch`.
copy_of : Str -> Str
copy_of = |path| "${scratch}/${Text.basename(path)}"

## Each plant's lines held to the findings: what is wrong, and how many marks
## there were.
check_marks! : List(Str), List(Finding) => { wrong : List(Str), marks : U64 }
check_marks! = |paths, findings| {
	var $wrong = []
	$marks : U64
	var $marks = 0
	for path in paths {
		$number : U64
		var $number = 0
		for line in Text.lines(Report.read_text!(path)) {
			$number = $number + 1
			number = $number
			key = "${path}:${number.to_str()}"
			got = findings
				.keep_if(|finding| finding.path == path and finding.line == number)
				.map(|finding| finding.check)
			match Checks.names.find_first(|check| line.ends_with("# ${check}")) {
				Ok(mark) => {
					$marks = $marks + 1
					if !(got.contains(mark)) {
						$wrong = $wrong.append("${key}: no ${mark} finding")
					}
					if got.len() > 1 {
						$wrong = $wrong.append("${key}: more than the one finding marked")
					}
				}
				Err(_) =>
					if !(got.is_empty()) {
						$wrong = $wrong.append("${key}: a finding (${Str.join_with(got, ", ")}) on a line not marked for one")
					}
			}
		}
	}
	{ wrong: $wrong, marks: $marks }
}

cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens/Checks.roc, 145 lines

## The four checks of find_extra_parens, over Roc's tree of a file: the
## parentheses and braceless `if`s that a code emitter leaves (the launcher,
## cookbook/roc/find_extra_parens.shale, says each rule). A finding names
## the node it stands on, so a rewrite (Edits) can take its brackets off.
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

Checks := [].{

	## A finding: its check, its line, and the place of the node it stands
	## on, counted from 1 as the tree counts.
	Found : { check : Str, line : U64, at : U64 }

	## The checks, in the order the summary counts them and a rewrite makes
	## them.
	names : List(Str)
	names = ["paren_if", "wrapped_body", "else_block", "lambda_if"]

	## Each finding in a file, node by node in the tree's order; at one node,
	## `wrapped_body`, `paren_if`, `else_block`, then `lambda_if`.
	## `source_lines` is the file's text split at each newline.
	findings_in : List(Tree.Node), List(Str) -> List(Checks.Found)
	findings_in = |nodes, source_lines| {
		var $found = []
		$place : U64
		var $place = 1
		for node in nodes {
			at = $place
			if wraps_body(nodes, at) {
				$found = $found.append({ check: "wrapped_body", line: node.line, at })
			}
			if Checks.is_paren_if(nodes, at) {
				$found = $found.append({ check: "paren_if", line: node.line, at })
			}
			if is_else_block(nodes, at) {
				$found = $found.append({ check: "else_block", line: node.line, at })
			}
			if is_lambda_if(nodes, at, source_lines) {
				$found = $found.append({ check: "lambda_if", line: node.line, at })
			}
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		$found
	}

	## Whether a node is a pair of parentheses: a one-item tuple.
	is_parens : Tree.Node -> Bool
	is_parens = |node| node.kind == "e-tuple" and node.kids.len() == 1

	## Whether a branch is a block, in braces.
	has_braces : Tree.Node -> Bool
	has_braces = |node| node.kind == "e-block"

	## Whether an `else` branch needs no braces added: it has them, or it is
	## the next `if` of an `else if`.
	else_is_braced : Tree.Node -> Bool
	else_is_braced = |otherwise|
		Checks.has_braces(otherwise) or otherwise.kind == "e-if-then-else"

	## Whether the node at `at` is an `if` with its condition wholly in
	## parentheses, or a branch with no braces.
	is_paren_if : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Bool
	is_paren_if = |nodes, at| {
		node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
		if node.kind != "e-if-then-else" {
			Bool.False
		} else {
			condition = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 1))
			then_branch = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 2))
			otherwise = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 3))
			Checks.is_parens(condition) or !(Checks.has_braces(then_branch)) or !(Checks.else_is_braced(otherwise))
		}
	}
}

## Whether the node at `at` is the last of its parent's kids.
is_last_kid : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Bool
is_last_kid = |nodes, at| {
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	Tree.last_kid(Tree.node_at(nodes, node.parent)) == at
}

## Whether parentheses at `at` wrap a whole body. The value of a declaration
## counts only over several lines; a statement counts wherever it stands, and
## `if`'s branches are paren_if's and the block's own.
wraps_body : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Bool
wraps_body = |nodes, at| {
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	if !(Checks.is_parens(node)) or node.parent == 0 {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		parent_kind = Tree.node_at(nodes, node.parent).kind
		if parent_kind == "statements" {
			Bool.True
		} else if parent_kind == "e-lambda" or parent_kind == "branch" {
			is_last_kid(nodes, at)
		} else if parent_kind == "s-decl" {
			is_last_kid(nodes, at) and node.end_line > node.line
		} else {
			Bool.False
		}
	}
}

## Whether the node at `at` is an `if` whose `else` is a block holding only
## another `if`: `else { if ... }`, which is `else if ...`.
is_else_block : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Bool
is_else_block = |nodes, at| {
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	if node.kind != "e-if-then-else" {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		otherwise = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 3))
		Checks.has_braces(otherwise) and holds_only_an_if(nodes, otherwise)
	}
}

## Whether a block's one statement is an `if`.
holds_only_an_if : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> Bool
holds_only_an_if = |nodes, block| {
	statements = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.first_kid(block))
	match statements.kids {
		[only] => Tree.node_at(nodes, only).kind == "e-if-then-else"
		_ => Bool.False
	}
}

## Whether the node at `at` is an `if` that is a lambda's whole body and
## shares its line with what comes before it, which can only be the lambda's
## `|`.
is_lambda_if : List(Tree.Node), U64, List(Str) -> Bool
is_lambda_if = |nodes, at, source_lines| {
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	if node.kind != "e-if-then-else" or node.parent == 0 {
		Bool.False
	} else if Tree.node_at(nodes, node.parent).kind != "e-lambda" or !(is_last_kid(nodes, at)) {
		Bool.False
	} else if Checks.is_paren_if(nodes, at) {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		line = Text.line_at(source_lines, node.line)
		before = Text.bytes_of(line, { start: 0, count: node.col - 1 })
		Text.trim(before) != ""
	}
}

## The edits that fix one check's findings in a file, made by the parser's
## spans, and the file's text with them made. Places in the text are counted
## from 1, as Shale's `sub` counts: an edit at `at` cuts `cut` bytes there and
## puts `put` in their place. A span the tree lacks, or two edits that
## overlap, is an `Err` saying so, which the caller stops the run with: a
## guess here would write braces into the wrong place.
import Checks
import lib.Tree

Edits := [].{

	## A file being rewritten: its path, its text's bytes and its tree.
	Source : { path : Str, text : List(U8), nodes : List(Tree.Node) }

	## One edit: `cut` bytes at `at` taken out, `put` put there.
	Edit : { at : U64, cut : U64, put : Str }

	## The edits that fix the findings of `check` among `findings`.
	for_check : Edits.Source, List(Checks.Found), Str -> Try(List(Edits.Edit), Str)
	for_check = |source, findings, check| {
		src = { path: source.path, text: source.text, nodes: source.nodes, starts: line_starts(source.text) }
		var $edits = []
		for finding in findings {
			if finding.check == check {
				$edits = $edits.concat(edits_of(src, finding)?)
			}
		}
		Ok($edits)
	}

	## The text with the edits made. At one place, an edit that only inserts
	## goes first, so that a closing brace nested in a branch's end stands
	## before the one that cuts the space after it; edits equal in both keep
	## their order.
	applied : List(U8), List(Edits.Edit) -> Try(List(U8), Str)
	applied = |text, edits| {
		var $numbered = []
		for edit in edits {
			$numbered = $numbered.append({ edit, number: $numbered.len() })
		}
		ordered = $numbered.sort_with(edit_order).map(|numbered| numbered.edit)
		var $pieces = []
		$from : U64
		var $from = 1
		for edit in ordered {
			if edit.at < $from {
				return Err("find_extra_parens: two edits overlap at index ${edit.at.to_str()}")
			}
			$pieces = $pieces.concat(span(text, $from, edit.at - 1)).concat(edit.put.to_utf8())
			$from = edit.at + edit.cut
		}
		Ok($pieces.concat(span(text, $from, text.len())))
	}
}

## A file being rewritten, with where each of its lines starts.
Src : { path : Str, text : List(U8), nodes : List(Tree.Node), starts : List(U64) }

## By place, then by what is cut, then by the order they were made in.
edit_order : { edit : Edits.Edit, number : U64 }, { edit : Edits.Edit, number : U64 } -> [Before, Same, After]
edit_order = |first, second|
	match compare(first.edit.at, second.edit.at) {
		Same =>
			match compare(first.edit.cut, second.edit.cut) {
				Same => compare(first.number, second.number)
				other => other
			}
		other => other
	}

compare : U64, U64 -> [Before, Same, After]
compare = |first, second|
	if first < second {
		Before
	} else if first > second {
		After
	} else {
		Same
	}

## The edits that fix one finding.
edits_of : Src, Checks.Found -> Try(List(Edits.Edit), Str)
edits_of = |src, finding| {
	nodes = src.nodes
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, finding.at)
	if finding.check == "wrapped_body" {
		inner = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.first_kid(node))
		Ok(bracket_removal(src, node, keeps_break(nodes, node, inner)))
	} else if finding.check == "else_block" {
		Ok(bracket_removal(src, Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 3)), Bool.False))
	} else if finding.check == "lambda_if" {
		from = start_of(src, finding.at)?
		after = before_space(src.text, from)
		Ok([{ at: after, cut: from - after, put: "\n" }])
	} else {
		paren_if_edits(src, node)
	}
}

## The edits that take an `if`'s condition out of its parentheses and put
## braces around each branch that has none.
paren_if_edits : Src, Tree.Node -> Try(List(Edits.Edit), Str)
paren_if_edits = |src, node| {
	nodes = src.nodes
	condition_at = Tree.kid_at(node, 1)
	then_at = Tree.kid_at(node, 2)
	otherwise_at = Tree.kid_at(node, 3)
	var $edits = []
	if Checks.is_parens(Tree.node_at(nodes, condition_at)) {
		$edits = $edits.concat(bracket_removal(src, Tree.node_at(nodes, condition_at), Bool.False))
	}
	if !(Checks.has_braces(Tree.node_at(nodes, then_at))) {
		$edits = $edits.append(opening_brace(src, then_at, end_of(src, condition_at)?)?)
		$edits = $edits.append(brace_before_else(src, then_at)?)
	}
	if !(Checks.else_is_braced(Tree.node_at(nodes, otherwise_at))) {
		after_else = past_else(src, end_of(src, then_at)?)?
		$edits = $edits.append(opening_brace(src, otherwise_at, after_else)?)
		$edits = $edits.append({ at: end_of(src, otherwise_at)?, cut: 0, put: " }" })
	}
	Ok($edits)
}

## Where each line starts in `text`, the first line at 1.
line_starts : List(U8) -> List(U64)
line_starts = |text| {
	var $starts = [1]
	$place : U64
	var $place = 1
	for byte in text {
		if byte == '\n' {
			$starts = $starts.append($place + 1)
		}
		$place = $place + 1
	}
	$starts
}

## The place of a line's column, both counted from 1.
offset_of : Src, U64, U64 -> U64
offset_of = |src, line, col| {
	start = match src.starts.get(line - 1) {
		Ok(found) => found
		Err(_) => crash "find_extra_parens: ${src.path} has no line ${line.to_str()}"
	}
	start + col - 1
}

## The byte at a place counted from 1, 0 past either end.
byte_at : List(U8), U64 -> U8
byte_at = |text, at|
	if at == 0 {
		0
	} else {
		text.get(at - 1) ?? 0
	}

## The bytes from place `from` to place `to`, both counted from 1 and kept
## inside the text, as Shale's `sub` takes them.
span : List(U8), U64, U64 -> List(U8)
span = |text, from, to| {
	start = if from < 1 {
		1
	} else {
		from
	}
	if to < start {
		[]
	} else {
		text.sublist({ start: start - 1, len: to + 1 - start })
	}
}

## Whether the bytes from `from` to `to` hold a `#`.
has_comment : List(U8), U64, U64 -> Bool
has_comment = |text, from, to| span(text, from, to).contains('#')

## Whether the bytes from `from` on spell `word`.
spells : List(U8), U64, Str -> Bool
spells = |text, from, word| span(text, from, from + word.count_utf8_bytes() - 1) == word.to_utf8()

is_space : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
is_space = |text, at| {
	byte = byte_at(text, at)
	byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\n'
}

## The first place at or past `at` that isn't white space.
past_space : List(U8), U64 -> U64
past_space = |text, at| {
	var $place = at
	while is_space(text, $place) {
		$place = $place + 1
	}
	$place
}

## The last place before `at` that isn't white space, plus one.
before_space : List(U8), U64 -> U64
before_space = |text, at| {
	var $place = at
	while $place > 1 and is_space(text, $place - 1) {
		$place = $place - 1
	}
	$place
}

## Where the line holding the place just before `at` starts.
last_line_start : List(U8), U64 -> U64
last_line_start = |text, at| {
	var $place = at - 1
	while $place > 1 and byte_at(text, $place - 1) != '\n' {
		$place = $place - 1
	}
	$place
}

## The first place at or past `at` outside white space and comments.
past_comments : List(U8), U64 -> U64
past_comments = |text, at| {
	var $place = past_space(text, at)
	while byte_at(text, $place) == '#' {
		while $place <= text.len() and byte_at(text, $place) != '\n' {
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		$place = past_space(text, $place)
	}
	$place
}

## The edits that take off the brackets at the ends of `node`: the space
## inside them goes too, so nothing is left of a line that held a bracket
## alone. With `keep_break`, the line break after the opening bracket stays,
## as a body on its own line wants. A comment beside a bracket keeps its line.
bracket_removal : Src, Tree.Node, Bool -> List(Edits.Edit)
bracket_removal = |src, node, keep_break| {
	text = src.text
	opening = offset_of(src, node.line, node.col)
	closing = offset_of(src, node.end_line, node.end_col) - 1
	past_opening = past_space(text, opening + 1)
	cut_to = if keep_break or byte_at(text, past_opening) == '#' {
		opening + 1
	} else {
		past_opening
	}
	before_closing = before_space(text, closing)
	cut_from = if has_comment(text, last_line_start(text, before_closing), before_closing - 1) {
		closing
	} else {
		before_closing
	}
	[
		{ at: opening, cut: cut_to - opening, put: "" },
		{ at: cut_from, cut: closing + 1 - cut_from, put: "" },
	]
}

## A body keeps its own line after `|x|`, `=>` or `=`, unless it is a block,
## whose brace sits there. A statement has nothing before it to keep.
keeps_break : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node, Tree.Node -> Bool
keeps_break = |nodes, node, inner|
	Tree.node_at(nodes, node.parent).kind != "statements" and inner.kind != "e-block"

no_span : Src, Tree.Node -> Try(U64, Str)
no_span = |src, node| Err("find_extra_parens: ${src.path}: can't find the ends of a ${node.kind}, which the tree gives no span")

## Where the node at `at` starts. Roc's tree gives a `match` and a unary
## operator no span of their own, so their ends are found from the nodes they
## hold; any other kind with no span is an `Err`.
start_of : Src, U64 -> Try(U64, Str)
start_of = |src, at| {
	node = Tree.node_at(src.nodes, at)
	if node.line != 0 {
		Ok(offset_of(src, node.line, node.col))
	} else if node.kind != "unary" and node.kind != "e-match" {
		no_span(src, node)
	} else {
		before = before_space(src.text, start_of(src, Tree.first_kid(node))?)
		if node.kind == "unary" {
			Ok(before - 1)
		} else if before > 5 and spells(src.text, before - 5, "match") {
			Ok(before - 5)
		} else {
			no_span(src, node)
		}
	}
}

## The place just past the node at `at`.
end_of : Src, U64 -> Try(U64, Str)
end_of = |src, at| {
	node = Tree.node_at(src.nodes, at)
	if node.line != 0 {
		Ok(offset_of(src, node.end_line, node.end_col))
	} else if node.kind == "unary" {
		end_of(src, Tree.first_kid(node))
	} else if node.kind != "e-match" {
		no_span(src, node)
	} else {
		branches = Tree.node_at(src.nodes, Tree.kid_at(node, 2))
		closing = past_comments(src.text, end_of(src, Tree.last_kid(branches))?)
		if byte_at(src.text, closing) == '}' {
			Ok(closing + 1)
		} else {
			no_span(src, node)
		}
	}
}

## The opening brace of the branch at `at`, on the line of what stands before
## it, which ends at `after`, since `roc fmt` keeps a line break before a
## brace. A comment there keeps its place after the brace.
opening_brace : Src, U64, U64 -> Try(Edits.Edit, Str)
opening_brace = |src, at, after| {
	from = start_of(src, at)?
	if has_comment(src.text, after, from - 1) {
		Ok({ at: after, cut: 0, put: " {" })
	} else {
		Ok({ at: after, cut: from - after, put: " { " })
	}
}

## The place just past the `else` that follows `then_end`.
past_else : Src, U64 -> Try(U64, Str)
past_else = |src, then_end| {
	at = past_comments(src.text, then_end)
	if spells(src.text, at, "else") {
		Ok(at + 4)
	} else {
		Err("find_extra_parens: ${src.path}: no `else` where a branch ended")
	}
}

## The closing brace of a `then` branch, with `else` brought up to it.
brace_before_else : Src, U64 -> Try(Edits.Edit, Str)
brace_before_else = |src, at| {
	to = end_of(src, at)?
	next_word = past_space(src.text, to)
	if spells(src.text, next_word, "else") {
		Ok({ at: to, cut: next_word - to, put: " } " })
	} else {
		Ok({ at: to, cut: 0, put: " }" })
	}
}
